papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has branched from simple soft-target matching into a family of methods including logits and feature matching, layer-wise and task-aware distillation, self- and online-distillation, data-free or adversarial sample synthesis, and strategies for low-precision or few-shot deployment. Practical success depends on matching the distilled signal to student capacity, handling limited or private data, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression tools (e.g., pruning and quantization). Open challenges remain around robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, preventing harmful bias transfer, and building stronger theoretical predictions of when and how distillation succeeds.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic into a central, practical toolkit for compressing large models and transferring behavior from high-capacity teachers into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and generative modeling, practitioners combine soft-label supervision, intermediate-representation matching, data- and privacy-aware strategies, and architecture-aware choices to trade accuracy for latency, memory, and power. KD is effective when paired with complementary techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, synthetic-data generation, curriculum schedules), but its success depends critically on what form of knowledge is distilled, how data or augmentations are used, and how teacher–student capacity and domain mismatches are managed. Remaining challenges include robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, mitigating bias transfer, and firm theoretical characterizations that predict when and how distillation will work in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable method for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD succeeds when its objectives, representation targets, and training regimes are chosen to match deployment constraints and student capacity; combining KD with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, data-free synthesis, and online protocols) extends its reach. However, KD also transfers risks (bias, privacy leakage, fragility) and faces limits when teacher signals are mismatched or training data are scarce, motivating task-aware design, robust distillation objectives, and emergent meta- and data-free methods.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied and practically effective set of methods for producing smaller, faster models from larger, high-capacity teachers. KD unifies a range of strategies—from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations and generating synthetic training data—and is commonly combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, data and augmentation strategies, and handling of domain shift or limited-data settings. The literature identifies both methodological extensions (multi-teacher fusion, online distillation, meta-learned teachers, data-free schemes) and recurring challenges (optimization mismatch, rare-token fidelity, privacy-aware transfer) that structure ongoing research and practical guidance.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Effective, Multifaceted, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their performance. KD operates via multiple knowledge channels — softened logits, intermediate feature matching, attention or relational signals, and ensemble or multi-teacher supervision — and it composes well with other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architectural replacement). Empirical results across vision, speech, and NLP show that carefully chosen distillation targets, student pre-training, data augmentation, and multi-teacher strategies reliably improve deployment trade-offs, but KD’s success depends on data availability, teacher–student alignment, and domain heterogeneity. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a flexible pipeline: design the student and distillation targets for the task and capacity of the student, use multi-source or ensemble teachers when appropriate, apply representation projection to reconcile mismatches, and explicitly evaluate under realistic data heterogeneity or deployment constraints to avoid hidden failures.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD transfers information beyond hard labels — including softened output distributions, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational signals — and is commonly combined with architectural or numerical compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD can yield large efficiency gains with modest performance loss when teacher–student design, data availability, and optimization dynamics are considered; however, its success is contingent on capacity alignment, data choices, and safeguards against transferring undesirable behaviors. Applications range from accelerated inference and edge deployment to domain adaptation, federated learning, and task-specific adaptations such as non-autoregressive translation and graph-to-MLP compression.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Challenges, and Empirical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a diverse set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Approaches extend beyond matching soft logits to include intermediate-feature mimicry, attention-driven layer alignment, many-to-many layer mapping, contrastive representation alignment, and task- or domain-aware search and adaptation. Empirical work shows KD is effective across modalities and tasks — from pre-trained language models and visual-linguistic systems to object detectors, recommender rankers, graph networks, and continual learning settings — but practical deployment requires addressing representation misalignment, task specificity, and catastrophic forgetting. This review synthesizes core strategies and key empirical findings to guide application and future research.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable framework for producing compact models by transferring behavior from larger teachers to smaller students. KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under resource constraints, and it extends beyond simple logit matching to include feature-level imitation, self-distillation, data-free strategies, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its efficacy depends on teacher quality and compatibility, the choice of distilled information, data availability, capacity mismatch, and fairness or robustness concerns. A considered KD pipeline—combining soft-targets, internal representation guidance, task-aware objectives, and suitable data strategies—yields robust, efficient students fitting real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students) to reduce inference cost and memory while retaining task performance. KD methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational or structural signals), how teachers and students are aligned (layer mappings, many-to-many correspondences), how data is used (original training data, synthetic or generated data, or no data), and how multiple teachers or online training regimes are incorporated. KD is routinely combined with architectural compression (pruning, quantization, and architecture search) and used across vision, language, graph, and generative-model settings. Empirical and practical work shows KD can produce compact models suitable for deployment, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful design of distillation objectives and training curricula.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of methods—logit (soft-target) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, layer- or module-alignment, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, progressive module replacement, online distillation, and data-free generative approaches—has been developed to address different deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, heterogeneous devices). Empirical work shows these techniques can substantially reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but success depends on student capacity, what is transferred, data availability, and task-specific alignment. Open challenges include robust transfer of rare-token behaviors, mitigating transfer of teacher biases, and scaling distillation to privacy- and resource-constrained or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches to Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques produce smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from larger or ensemble teachers to compact students. Across modalities and tasks, researchers have developed diverse strategies—teacher–student logits matching, layer-wise representation matching, adversarial sample generation, progressive module replacement, many-to-many layer mapping, and task-aware filtering—to address capacity gaps, data access limits, privacy constraints, and robustness needs. Practical deployments additionally combine distillation with pruning, structured sparsity, and federated protocols to meet hardware and communication budgets. Empirical work shows that careful design of distillation objectives and inputs can preserve most of the teacher’s accuracy and even transfer properties such as adversarial robustness, while specialized schemes enable distillation without original training data or across continual/heterogeneous settings.

papers_seen.author: Cardenas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable family of methods for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD can preserve most of a teacher’s performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints; it is applied across modalities (vision, language, speech, multimodal) and is routinely combined with complementary compression techniques. However, KD’s benefits depend strongly on choices about what is distilled (logits, features, attention, relational structure), teacher–student compatibility, data availability (including data-free settings), and deployment constraints; addressing domain shift, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, and avoiding undesirable property transfer remain important open challenges. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central component of modern compression pipelines while recognizing its context-dependent limits and recommending pragmatic combinations with other compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Mechanisms, and Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students suitable for production. KD methods span soft-label transfer, representation- and layer-level matching, adversarial and privacy-aware variants, and meta- or teacher-adaptive strategies. When combined with appropriate pre-training, architecture-aware adapters, and task-aware objectives, distillation yields compact models that approach teacher performance under realistic compute, data, and deployment constraints. However, outcomes depend on teacher–student compatibility, what signals are distilled, and whether robustness or privacy guarantees are required.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Strategies, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, pragmatic technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When applied deliberately — choosing what form of knowledge to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle data and deployment constraints — KD routinely yields favorable tradeoffs between model compactness and retained performance. However, distillation is not automatic: data availability, teacher–student mismatches, and application-specific constraints (latency, privacy, heterogeneity) shape both achievable gains and failure modes. Best practice therefore combines representation-aware objectives, curriculum or annealing schedules, multi-teacher or ensemble guidance where helpful, and deployment-aware mechanisms such as data-free generation or privacy-preserving aggregation to realize robust, efficient students.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and selected internal information from teacher models. A diverse set of distillation objectives and training regimes—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature or attention alignment, multi-teacher and ensemble supervision, adversarial or data-free variants, and task- or device-aware architecture search—enable substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data and augmentation, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques; open problems remain in theoretical explanation, cross-distribution robustness, and preserving rare-token or fairness-sensitive behavior.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from larger or more informative models (teachers) into smaller or more efficient models (students). Research across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks has developed multiple KD objectives (soft-label matching, intermediate layer alignment, contrastive/representation losses), training regimes (offline teacher-student, online co-training, meta-learned teacher updates), and architecture-aware compression strategies (channel-wise attention, task-adaptive architecture search). Empirical and theoretical work highlights tradeoffs between bias and variance introduced by soft targets, the value of pre-training compact models before distillation, and the importance of data and augmentation choices for effective transfer. Emerging large-scale and privacy-aware deployments leverage online and federated distillation variants to reduce communication and improve reproducibility, while new approaches aim to make teachers more student-friendly or distill internal representations rather than only outputs. Key open challenges include matching representational structure across heterogeneous architectures, choosing what and when to distill, and scaling methods to very large datasets and distributed settings while preserving privacy and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques provide a set of complementary strategies to transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller student models. Methods span matching output distributions (soft targets), imitating intermediate representations and attention, aligning layers, using multiple teachers or self-teaching schedules, and applying task- or data-aware procedures including data-free generation and low-precision adaptation. Empirical work shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance while gaining speed and memory efficiency, but outcomes depend on which knowledge is transferred, student capacity, data availability, and task specificity. Practical deployments combine distillation with architecture search, quantization, and curriculum or augmentation strategies to balance fidelity, robustness, and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a versatile and practically effective approach for compressing large deep models into compact ones that are suitable for deployment. Across NLP, speech, vision-language, and specialized tasks such as machine reading comprehension, KD enables students to inherit performance-critical behaviors from larger teachers while enabling orders-of-magnitude reductions in model size and compute. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., architecture search or structured pruning) and when tailored to task or domain specifics, distillation yields compressed models that approach teacher performance while meeting resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Principled Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical technique for compressing large neural models into deployable, efficient students while preserving much of teacher performance. Across supervised, self-supervised, multi-task, and low-precision settings, distillation can recover large-model accuracy in smaller footprints when combined with careful design choices that address capacity mismatch, task relevance, and the nature of the transferred knowledge. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on distillation schedule, selection of what to transfer (logits, features, or task-aware subsets), and occasionally on teacher improvement or specialization. Understanding these interactions is key to robust compression for production NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical First-Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically proven approach for compressing large models into smaller, efficient students while preserving much of task performance. KD methods—ranging from soft-label matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online variants, and data-free techniques—enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation has well-documented failure modes (e.g., propagation of teacher errors, optimization mismatch) that require careful teacher/student design, data strategies, and complementary methods to get reliable results in practice.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has evolved from logit-matching for model compression into a multifaceted toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, attention- and channel-level transfers, teacher ensembles, data- and teacher-free variants, and task- or domain-aware adaptations. Practical success depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student alignment (capacity and architecture), the availability and provenance of data, and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design). While KD often preserves much of the teacher’s performance and can improve generalization through soft-target regularization, important limits remain around distribution shift, low-frequency token or class handling, and preserving robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression methods have become central tools for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the accuracy and capabilities of large teachers. Research over the past decade has produced a diverse set of techniques—ranging from distilling logits, internal representations, and attention patterns to data-free and few-shot strategies, multi-teacher ensembles, and task-adaptive search for student architectures. These approaches have been applied across vision, language, multimodal, and deployed/distributed settings, demonstrating substantial gains in inference speed and model size while exposing trade-offs in robustness, data requirements, and modality alignment. This survey summarizes the main algorithmic families, common engineering strategies, notable empirical outcomes, and key open challenges for applying distillation in practice.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods transfer information from larger, more expensive models to smaller, cheaper models to reduce inference cost while retaining accuracy. Across computer vision, speech, recommender systems and natural language processing, KD variants have targeted soft-label transfer, relational or feature imitation, self-distillation, and teacher adaptation to improve student generalization. Practical work emphasizes complementary strategies — pretraining compact architectures, specialist teacher training, careful input augmentation, and training-time efficiency — to address optimization mismatch, domain shift, and computational overhead. Remaining challenges include imperfect matching between teacher and student distributions, choosing data and augmentation strategies that preserve useful teacher signals, and designing distillation procedures that scale to constrained hardware and domain-specific needs.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, System-Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact student models that preserve much of a larger teacher’s accuracy while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. KD succeeds most reliably when treated as a system-level design choice rather than a single auxiliary loss: practitioners should choose what signals to transfer (logits, features, attention, relations), align student and teacher architectures, incorporate complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and address data limitations through augmentation or data-free/federated strategies. KD has proven value across modalities but also carries risks — optimization difficulties, teacher errors propagated to students, and sensitivity to available data — that require explicit mitigation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Current Understandings of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used model compression paradigm in which a smaller student model is trained to capture the behavior of a larger teacher model. It has been applied across domains (vision, NLP, recommender systems, medical imaging) to reduce model size and latency while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Work in the field explores what is transferred (soft outputs, internal representations, feature relations), how to improve transfer (adversarial samples, contrastive objectives, structural transformations), and how to address practical constraints (absence of original data, domain shift, privacy, fairness and robustness). Empirical results show KD often yields substantial memory and runtime benefits with modest accuracy loss and can be combined with pruning, quantization and architecture search. Yet KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, imperfect teacher signals, and mismatches between teacher and student capacity can limit how closely a student matches a teacher; research continues into theoretical explanations and robust, data-efficient methods.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and pragmatic framework for compressing large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, or more private models across modalities and tasks. When applied thoughtfully — by matching outputs, intermediate representations, training dynamics, or ensembles — KD can preserve or even improve task performance while enabling low-latency inference, reduced memory/compute, and new deployment modes (e.g., federated, data-free, or low-precision). However, distillation is not automatic: design choices about what to transfer, when to transfer, and how to align teacher and student matter for robustness, domain shifts, and rare-token behavior. I argue that best practice combines representation-aware objectives, selective or collaborative teaching strategies, and deployment-aware constraints (privacy, communication, numeric precision) to realize the full benefits of distillation in NLP and other deep learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic into a practical, multi-purpose toolkit for compressing large models while preserving performance across domains and modalities. KD enables deployment of powerful models on resource-constrained devices, supports domain adaptation, helps preserve privacy, and can be adapted to architectures ranging from transformers to GANs and GNNs. Complementary techniques — e.g., architectural replacement, data augmentation, multi-teacher schemes, and precision reduction — expand KD’s effectiveness. However, KD’s success depends on how knowledge is represented and transferred (logits, internal representations, relations) and on availability or synthesis of appropriate data. The balance of method and setting determines whether KD yields compact models that meet real-world constraints without unacceptable loss of fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First-Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students. It transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students, producing models that preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost and memory. KD is broadly applicable across modalities and tasks, and its practical success increases when combined with complementary techniques (e.g., architecture search, pruning, representation matching) and when training pipelines are adapted to data availability, privacy constraints, and teacher–student mismatches. However, KD is not universally sufficient: distributional shifts, data heterogeneity, absence of training data, and poorly chosen teacher signals can limit effectiveness, so careful design choices and hybrid pipelines are recommended.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, more expressive models to smaller, efficient models to enable practical deployment without excessive loss in performance. These methods include matching teacher soft outputs, feature-level alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and architecture-aware strategies for heterogeneous settings. Across domains—vision, speech, NLP, and recommender systems—distillation is used both to compress models for latency and memory constraints and to inject complementary knowledge (e.g., cross-task or cross-modal signals). Empirical work shows that careful design choices (e.g., mixing hard/soft targets, projector modules, or student-aware teacher training) and task-specific adaptations address common pitfalls such as information loss on rare tokens or domain shifts. Open directions include stronger theoretical understanding, robustness under imperfect teachers, and principled integration with quantization, federated settings, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Rationale, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a practical, broadly applicable pathway to compress large neural models into smaller students that retain much of teacher performance. As a flexible toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD supports a range of transfer signals (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention and relational signals), and it integrates naturally with complementary compression mechanisms (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment constraints (latency, privacy, heterogeneity). KD delivers strong empirical gains across modalities and tasks when matched to student capacity and data conditions, but it is not a universal fix: success requires careful teacher–student design, data and curriculum strategies, and safeguards for distribution shift and rare-token fidelity. The position taken here is that KD should be treated as a first‑line, default strategy for model compression in deep learning and NLP—used proactively and in combination with other compression primitives—while acknowledging its failure modes and design requirements.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression methods transfer knowledge from larger, high-capacity models to smaller, efficient models to reduce inference cost and memory while preserving performance. Approaches span soft-label (logit) matching, feature- or attention-level imitation, multi-teacher fusion, data-free distillation, and adaptations for domain shift and heterogeneous deployment. Empirical results show distilled students can approach or match teacher performance in many settings, but success depends on teacher quality, the form of transferred knowledge, training curricula, and application-specific design choices. Emerging theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and reveal practical tradeoffs such as bias–variance effects of soft labels and the roles of ensemble and self-distillation.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful and practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD should be treated not as a single loss term but as a system-level design primitive that is chosen and tuned to match teacher–student capacity, data availability, deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy), and architectural heterogeneity. When designed with appropriate distilled signals, data strategies (including data-free synthesis), projector or alignment modules, and complementary compression techniques, distillation reliably enables compact, efficient models for real-world NLP and deep-learning applications. However, careful attention to teacher quality, student capacity, optimization dynamics, and domain shift is required to avoid failure modes and degraded behavior.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large, high-performance models into smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from a teacher to a student. Recent work spans many complementary strategies — logit/soft-target matching, feature and layer-wise distillation, structural and channel-level transformations, data-free generation of proxy inputs, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and task-aware filtering — and addresses practical concerns such as cross-domain transfer, limited compute, and maintaining task performance in NLP settings. Progress includes specialized algorithms for pre-trained language model compression, algorithmic and architectural enhancements that reduce capacity gaps, and theoretical analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. Together these developments offer a toolkit for deploying compact models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive environments while preserving most of the original model performance.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost while retaining performance. A broad family of approaches—from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate-feature imitation, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free synthesis, and federated or privacy-aware protocols—enables deployment across vision, speech, and language tasks. Practical success depends on matching the distillation signal to student capacity, combining KD with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, pretraining), and addressing data, optimization, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer information from larger, more expensive models (teachers) into smaller, cheaper models (students) to reduce inference cost, enable deployment in constrained environments, or impart desirable properties such as robustness or interpretability. Across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks, researchers have developed a spectrum of KD strategies — from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate features, attention, or relational signals — and combined these with architecture-level compression, pretraining, and data-management strategies. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often approach teacher performance, but success depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation target, data availability, and training dynamics. Open problems include reliable distillation without original data, transferring inductive biases and robustness, and handling heterogeneous or federated data and models.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches and Insights in Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer useful information from larger, more expensive models (or ensembles) to smaller, deployable models. Research spans theoretical analyses of what is transferred, architectural and loss-design strategies to improve feature and output matching, specialized teacher–student training regimes (including multi-teacher and student-aware teacher training), online and federated distillation for large-scale or privacy-sensitive settings, and structural compression strategies that preserve accuracy while reducing memory and compute. Applications include image models, generative models, question-answering systems and multi-task natural language understanding, with methods tailored to domain constraints such as heterogeneous device capabilities and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression — Powerful but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, empirically validated strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD works through a range of mechanisms (soft targets, intermediate representation matching, teacher ensembles, and data‑side interventions) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and careful attention to teacher–student alignment, data provenance, and deployment constraints. While KD often yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs, practitioners must treat it as a context‑sensitive tool and follow best practices to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors or encountering failure modes under limited data, heterogeneity, or privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across NLP, speech, vision, and recommendation systems, KD reduces inference cost and memory, enables deployment on constrained devices, and can transfer specialized capabilities when paired with appropriate data and training choices. Its effectiveness depends on what is distilled (soft targets, intermediate features, relational signals), the availability and synthesis of training data, and teacher–student design; complementary compression tools and safeguards addressing bias, privacy, and distributional mismatch are often required for robust, real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. The field comprises a family of methods that transfer different forms of information—from soft logits to internal representations, attention maps, and relational structure—and integrates naturally with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Success depends on choosing what to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacities and architectures, managing data availability (including data-free or federated setups), and designing appropriate optimization curricula. While KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, important limitations remain around teacher–student mismatch, domain shift, rare-token preservation in NLP, and robustness under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring useful predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, KD variants—ranging from soft-target matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware approaches—enable substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher and student design, data and augmentation strategies, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, low-precision numerics). When these components are co-designed, distilled models can approach teacher-level performance and support real-world, resource-constrained deployments, though open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, rare-token fidelity, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable framework for producing compact models by transferring behavior from larger teachers to smaller students. KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under resource constraints, and it extends beyond simple logit matching to include feature-level imitation, self-distillation, data-free strategies, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its efficacy depends on teacher quality and compatibility, the choice of distilled information, data availability, capacity mismatch, and fairness or robustness concerns. A considered KD pipeline—combining soft-targets, internal representation guidance, task-aware objectives, and suitable data strategies—yields robust, efficient students fitting real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features/attention, relational or structural signals) and can be applied in offline, online, ensemble, or data-constrained settings. Empirical results across vision, speech, and language show that appropriately designed distillation pipelines can deliver large efficiency gains with modest loss (and sometimes gains) in accuracy, but success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, data availability, and deployment constraints. Practical deployments typically combine KD with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and require design attention to robustness, domain shift, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining as much task performance as possible. Over the past decade KD has evolved from matching softened output distributions to a broad set of practical techniques that include intermediate representation matching, layer-wise alignment, online and multi-teacher training, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning and quantization. Empirical work shows KD can substantially shrink model size and latency for vision and language systems and can be adapted for privacy-sensitive and distributed settings; however, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and the availability or synthesis of suitable training data, and it faces open challenges in robustness, cross-domain generalization, and heterogeneous deployment.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Open Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, cheaper students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, methods range from classic teacher-student logits supervision to data-free and online schemes, meta-learned teachers, and representation-level transfers. Empirical work shows KD often yields substantial efficiency gains but its effectiveness depends on dataset complexity, model capacity, data availability, and optimization choices; important failure modes and practical remediation strategies have been identified.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models by transferring information from high-capacity teachers to smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while retaining much of the teacher performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded from logits-based soft-target matching to a rich family of techniques including feature- and attention-level alignment, relational and representation matching, student-aware teacher design, and integration with architecture search and other compression primitives. Empirical work across vision and language shows KD both as a route to practical deployment of pre-trained transformers and as a general regularizer that can improve student generalization; ongoing challenges include aligning heterogeneous architectures, coping with limited or private data, and preserving performance on rare classes or tokens. This article synthesizes core methods, mechanistic explanations, practical adaptations for NLP, and directions where KD currently has the greatest impact.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has branched from simple soft-target matching into a family of methods including logits and feature matching, layer-wise and task-aware distillation, self- and online-distillation, data-free or adversarial sample synthesis, and strategies for low-precision or few-shot deployment. Practical success depends on matching the distilled signal to student capacity, handling limited or private data, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression tools (e.g., pruning and quantization). Open challenges remain around robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, preventing harmful bias transfer, and building stronger theoretical predictions of when and how distillation succeeds.

papers_seen.author: Rasmussen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with task-aware choices for what and how to transfer (soft labels, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), and when combined with complementary compression strategies (architecture adaptation, pruning, quantization, data augmentation or synthesis), KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student alignment, availability or synthesis of appropriate data, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy risks. Practical compression pipelines therefore treat distillation as a core tool whose design must be tailored to the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable smaller, faster models to inherit performance characteristics from larger models. Research has introduced multiple KD paradigms—teacher-student soft-label transfer, self-distillation, feature/internal-representation matching, multi-teacher strategies, and data-augmentation–aware distillation—each addressing different practical constraints such as domain shift, resource limits, or heterogeneous architectures. Applications span speech, machine translation evaluation, ASR, and domain-specific pretrained models; empirical work shows substantial reductions in model size and latency can be achieved with modest accuracy loss, or sometimes even gains, when distillation is combined with architectural adaptations and training-time strategies. Remaining challenges include transferring internal representations across heterogeneous architectures, choosing or designing teachers that are most useful for particular students, and preserving low-frequency or domain-specific signals during aggressive compression.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses or transfers knowledge from larger, more expensive models (teachers) into smaller, cheaper models (students) by using richer supervision than hard labels alone. The literature has developed multiple complementary strategies—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, architecturally guided replacement, multi-teacher schedules, data- and privacy-aware variants, and teacher-training schemes—to address deployment constraints, domain shift, and limited or private data. Empirical work shows these approaches can close much of the performance gap to full-size models across classification, language understanding, and retrieval tasks; theoretical and empirical analyses explain why distillation often improves generalization beyond mere compression. Remaining challenges include input distribution mismatch, low-frequency token fidelity in sequence tasks, and robust distillation without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Work across vision and language shows a set of recurring strategies: transfer using softened outputs (soft targets), imitation of intermediate/internal representations, layer mapping between teacher and student, task-adaptive architecture search, self-distillation, and data-free distillation when original training data are unavailable. Empirical results indicate that properly designed distillation can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while offering large gains in inference speed and memory; however, success depends on which knowledge is transferred (outputs vs. internal features), how layers are aligned, and whether task specificity and data availability are addressed. The field currently balances practical engineering (architecture and search) with algorithmic refinements (losses and training regimes), and open challenges include robust data-free methods, principled many-to-many layer matching, and teacher designs that are optimized to be “student-friendly.”
