papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Current Understandings of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used model compression paradigm in which a smaller student model is trained to capture the behavior of a larger teacher model. It has been applied across domains (vision, NLP, recommender systems, medical imaging) to reduce model size and latency while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Work in the field explores what is transferred (soft outputs, internal representations, feature relations), how to improve transfer (adversarial samples, contrastive objectives, structural transformations), and how to address practical constraints (absence of original data, domain shift, privacy, fairness and robustness). Empirical results show KD often yields substantial memory and runtime benefits with modest accuracy loss and can be combined with pruning, quantization and architecture search. Yet KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, imperfect teacher signals, and mismatches between teacher and student capacity can limit how closely a student matches a teacher; research continues into theoretical explanations and robust, data-efficient methods.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques seek to reduce the runtime, memory, and deployment costs of large deep models while retaining their predictive performance or improving other desiderata (e.g., interpretability, fairness). Across vision and language domains, methods range from classical teacher-to-student soft-target distillation to transferring intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, selective sample-driven distillation, and teacher-adaptive or teacher-free schemes. Empirical work shows that carefully chosen distillation targets, alignment of intermediate representations, and input-side practices (such as tailored data augmentation) can materially affect student performance. Remaining challenges include representation mismatches between teacher and student, identifying which training samples are beneficial for transfer, and adapting distillation to domain- or resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high‑performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring useful information from teachers. Techniques vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), how teachers are chosen or ensembled, and whether distillation is done with or without access to original data. Practical deployments combine distillation with complementary strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture design, data augmentation, or synthetic-data generation) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While distillation often preserves much of teacher performance, success depends on careful objective design, alignment of teacher and student capacity, data strategies, and mitigation of failure modes such as degraded handling of low‑frequency tokens, adversarial vulnerability, or erased relative class information.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Principled Use of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, practical method for compressing large models into smaller, efficient students while retaining much of teacher performance. However, its success is conditional: choices about what to transfer, how to supervise internal representations, how to design student architectures for particular tasks, and how to handle data, distribution shift, and fairness constraints materially affect outcomes. I argue that KD should be treated as a flexible design pattern—combining soft-target transfer, internal-representation matching, task-adaptive architecture design, and explicit fairness or data strategies—to produce reliable, deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and selected internal information from teacher models. A diverse set of distillation objectives and training regimes—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature or attention alignment, multi-teacher and ensemble supervision, adversarial or data-free variants, and task- or device-aware architecture search—enable substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data and augmentation, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques; open problems remain in theoretical explanation, cross-distribution robustness, and preserving rare-token or fairness-sensitive behavior.

papers_seen.author: Carpenter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Backbone of Model Compression: Capabilities, Variants, and Contextual Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD supports a broad set of objectives—matching logits, aligning internal representations, using online or multi-teacher schemes, and operating with or without original training data—so it serves as the backbone of many modern compression pipelines. However, its success is context-dependent: choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data availability, and deployment constraints determine outcomes, and KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques and principled training workflows.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Tradeoffs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses or transfers behaviors of larger or differently structured models into smaller or alternative models by training students to match teacher outputs, intermediate representations, or other derived supervision signals. Empirically, distillation improves deployment efficiency, can transfer inductive biases and robustness properties, and enables compression across domains including classification, generation, speech, and transformers. Success depends on choices such as what to transfer (logits, features, attention, or synthetic labels), how to combine hard and soft targets, privacy/robustness constraints, and whether teachers are perfect. Contemporary work links distillation to regularization and label smoothing, proposes layer-level and adversarial methods, and demonstrates broad applicability while highlighting limitations tied to teacher quality, data distribution, and adversarial vulnerability.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Principled Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' predictive power. KD is most effective when it goes beyond naïve soft-label copying: matching internal representations, aligning inputs and tokenization, choosing appropriate data or synthesis strategies, and adapting teacher updates or curricula all materially affect transfer quality. KD should be used as part of a broader compression pipeline (architecture design, quantization, pruning, or data strategies) and with explicit checks for rare-token behavior, fairness, and robustness. When applied with these considerations, KD reliably produces compact models suitable for production constraints in vision, language, and other modalities.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from larger, richer teacher models to smaller, cheaper student models to enable deployment under compute, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature encompasses simple soft-label matching, richer supervision signals that align intermediate features or attention, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-preserving designs, and combinations with structural compression such as pruning and layer skipping. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation can both compress and regularize models, but effectiveness depends on teacher-student mismatch, data availability, and optimization choices; practical pipelines therefore combine multiple compression mechanisms, careful signal selection, and task-aware adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. When treated as a system-level primitive rather than a single loss term, KD can be adapted to data availability, deployment constraints, and student–teacher mismatch to produce compact models that retain much of teachers' performance. Practical application of KD involves choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention, relational signals), how to expose students to informative inputs (real, synthesized, or online predictions), and how to combine KD with complementary compression methods and privacy-preserving protocols. Despite strong empirical success, KD has known failure modes tied to teacher errors, limited data, and distribution shift that require targeted mitigations and principled design.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: The Strengths and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large models into deployable, efficient students across modalities. Empirical work shows KD can preserve task performance while drastically reducing size and compute, but its success depends on choices of what and how to transfer, availability and provenance of data, and training dynamics. Advances in feature-matching, progressive module replacement, task-aware layer selection, data-free synthesis, and robustness-aware distillation expand KD's applicability but do not eliminate core challenges—optimization barriers, distribution heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and potential transfer of unwanted behaviors. A careful, task-aware combination of techniques is therefore required to realize reliable, compact models for production use.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Strategy for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a niche compression trick into a unifying strategy that addresses model size, inference latency, domain shifts, multimodal transfer, privacy, and training efficiency. By transferring supervisory signals, intermediate representations, or relational structure from larger or more capable systems, KD enables compact student models to retain much of the performance of cumbersome teachers while meeting practical deployment constraints. When combined with task-aware architecture search, layer-mapping techniques, and online or domain-aware protocols, distillation offers a principled path to build small, fast, and adaptable models across diverse settings.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central Tool for Practical Model Compression, with Limits and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. When combined with complementary strategies—such as intermediate-feature alignment, architecture-aware design, data-aware selection, and data-free synthesis—distillation enables practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. However, KD is not universally sufficient: careful choice of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data or domain mismatch is required to avoid propagating errors or losing robustness.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from large teacher models or ensembles to smaller student models to reduce inference cost and memory while preserving task performance. The field encompasses soft-label (logit) supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, structural and architectural transformations, data-free and privacy-aware variants, multi-teacher and online distillation, and meta-learned teacher strategies. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often improves student generalization and enables deployment under resource constraints, but outcomes depend strongly on what signals are transferred, data availability and provenance, optimization dynamics, and teacher–student capacity gaps. Practical deployment requires choosing student architectures, distillation signals, and training regimes aligned to the target task and constraints; key open problems include robust data-free distillation, principled teacher design, and theoretical characterization of when different knowledge sources help.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. Practitioners apply KD not only as a logits-matching loss but as a system-level design primitive that includes representation matching, multi-teacher fusion, data and curriculum design, and combination with pruning and quantization. Its empirical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (soft labels, intermediate features, relational signals), how to map teacher signals to potentially heterogeneous students, and how to handle limited or private data. While KD often yields compact models with near-teacher performance and useful regularization effects, limitations remain: imperfect teacher signals, optimization challenges, robustness and fairness transfer, and domain-shift or data-scarce scenarios. Current best practices emphasize task-aware selection of distilled signals, layer/projector alignment, and hybrid pipelines that combine KD with other compression techniques to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied and practically effective set of methods for producing smaller, faster models from larger, high-capacity teachers. KD unifies a range of strategies—from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations and generating synthetic training data—and is commonly combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, data and augmentation strategies, and handling of domain shift or limited-data settings. The literature identifies both methodological extensions (multi-teacher fusion, online distillation, meta-learned teachers, data-free schemes) and recurring challenges (optimization mismatch, rare-token fidelity, privacy-aware transfer) that structure ongoing research and practical guidance.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. Across vision and language tasks, KD has been adapted beyond simple soft-label matching to include intermediate-feature supervision, layer- or module-level mapping, selective sample transfer, data-free synthesis, and combinations with other compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical deployments reveal important dependencies on teacher quality, student architecture, data availability, and training protocols; when these are handled deliberately, distilled models can achieve strong trade-offs in accuracy, latency, and resource use. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data heterogeneity, preserving low-frequency or rare outputs, and aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures in privacy-sensitive or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods transfer information from larger, more expensive models to smaller, cheaper models to reduce inference cost while retaining accuracy. Across computer vision, speech, recommender systems and natural language processing, KD variants have targeted soft-label transfer, relational or feature imitation, self-distillation, and teacher adaptation to improve student generalization. Practical work emphasizes complementary strategies — pretraining compact architectures, specialist teacher training, careful input augmentation, and training-time efficiency — to address optimization mismatch, domain shift, and computational overhead. Remaining challenges include imperfect matching between teacher and student distributions, choosing data and augmentation strategies that preserve useful teacher signals, and designing distillation procedures that scale to constrained hardware and domain-specific needs.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Tradeoffs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses or transfers behaviors of larger or differently structured models into smaller or alternative models by training students to match teacher outputs, intermediate representations, or other derived supervision signals. Empirically, distillation improves deployment efficiency, can transfer inductive biases and robustness properties, and enables compression across domains including classification, generation, speech, and transformers. Success depends on choices such as what to transfer (logits, features, attention, or synthetic labels), how to combine hard and soft targets, privacy/robustness constraints, and whether teachers are perfect. Contemporary work links distillation to regularization and label smoothing, proposes layer-level and adversarial methods, and demonstrates broad applicability while highlighting limitations tied to teacher quality, data distribution, and adversarial vulnerability.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, more expressive models to smaller, efficient models to enable practical deployment without excessive loss in performance. These methods include matching teacher soft outputs, feature-level alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and architecture-aware strategies for heterogeneous settings. Across domains—vision, speech, NLP, and recommender systems—distillation is used both to compress models for latency and memory constraints and to inject complementary knowledge (e.g., cross-task or cross-modal signals). Empirical work shows that careful design choices (e.g., mixing hard/soft targets, projector modules, or student-aware teacher training) and task-specific adaptations address common pitfalls such as information loss on rare tokens or domain shifts. Open directions include stronger theoretical understanding, robustness under imperfect teachers, and principled integration with quantization, federated settings, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has branched from simple soft-target matching into a family of methods including logits and feature matching, layer-wise and task-aware distillation, self- and online-distillation, data-free or adversarial sample synthesis, and strategies for low-precision or few-shot deployment. Practical success depends on matching the distilled signal to student capacity, handling limited or private data, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression tools (e.g., pruning and quantization). Open challenges remain around robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, preventing harmful bias transfer, and building stronger theoretical predictions of when and how distillation succeeds.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques seek to reduce the runtime, memory, and deployment costs of large deep models while retaining their predictive performance or improving other desiderata (e.g., interpretability, fairness). Across vision and language domains, methods range from classical teacher-to-student soft-target distillation to transferring intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, selective sample-driven distillation, and teacher-adaptive or teacher-free schemes. Empirical work shows that carefully chosen distillation targets, alignment of intermediate representations, and input-side practices (such as tailored data augmentation) can materially affect student performance. Remaining challenges include representation mismatches between teacher and student, identifying which training samples are beneficial for transfer, and adapting distillation to domain- or resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: The Pragmatic Power and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured into a practical toolkit for shrinking models, transferring behavior across architectures and modalities, and enabling deployment under compute, memory, or privacy constraints. Beyond straightforward teacher-to-student compression, distillation techniques combine with data augmentation, synthetic-data generation, and regularization to address limited data, cross-domain gaps, and interpretability needs. However, outcomes depend on choices about teacher quality, training data availability, and objective design; careful method selection is required to realize reliable, production-ready gains.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, high-impact approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD succeeds because it can transfer diverse forms of information—soft outputs, internal representations, relational structure—and because it composes naturally with complementary techniques (pretraining, pruning, quantization, data augmentation, and multi-teacher ensembles). When applied with attention to teacher quality, data alignment, and student pretraining, KD enables practical, resource-aware deployments across vision, speech, and language tasks. This paper argues KD should often be the first method considered for compression, and outlines core mechanisms, practical recipes, and remaining challenges for robust application in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods transfer information from larger, more expensive models to smaller, cheaper models to reduce inference cost while retaining accuracy. Across computer vision, speech, recommender systems and natural language processing, KD variants have targeted soft-label transfer, relational or feature imitation, self-distillation, and teacher adaptation to improve student generalization. Practical work emphasizes complementary strategies — pretraining compact architectures, specialist teacher training, careful input augmentation, and training-time efficiency — to address optimization mismatch, domain shift, and computational overhead. Remaining challenges include imperfect matching between teacher and student distributions, choosing data and augmentation strategies that preserve useful teacher signals, and designing distillation procedures that scale to constrained hardware and domain-specific needs.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation can be combined with architectural replacement, layer mapping, and task-adaptive search to produce compact models that meet latency and capacity constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend strongly on teacher quality, data complexity, and which examples or representations are used for transfer; naive application can propagate teacher errors or harm low-frequency predictions. Careful design—using task-aware compression, selective or mixed supervision, and targeted remedies for dataset artifacts—enables distillation to deliver efficient, robust models for real-world NLP and vision systems.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression — Powerful but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, empirically validated strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD works through a range of mechanisms (soft targets, intermediate representation matching, teacher ensembles, and data‑side interventions) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and careful attention to teacher–student alignment, data provenance, and deployment constraints. While KD often yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs, practitioners must treat it as a context‑sensitive tool and follow best practices to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors or encountering failure modes under limited data, heterogeneity, or privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and complementary model-compression techniques transfer behaviors of large models into smaller, more efficient models by supervising students with information derived from teachers (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention, or synthetic labels). Empirical results across vision, speech, and language show that carefully designed distillation pipelines can preserve much of a teacher’s performance while reducing size and latency. Effective practice combines choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data strategies (including augmentation or synthesis), and complementary structural compression. Remaining challenges include handling imperfect teachers, limited or private data, robustness and out-of-distribution behavior, and principled automation of trade-offs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable tool for shrinking large deep models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. When combined with complementary practices — careful teacher selection or adaptation, pre-training of compact architectures, feature-level matching, and privacy- or data-aware workflows — KD yields most of the practical benefits of compression while exposing clear trade-offs and failure modes. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the backbone of model compression pipelines, but that realizing reliable production gains requires principled choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression methods transfer knowledge from larger, high-capacity models to smaller, efficient models to reduce inference cost and memory while preserving performance. Approaches span soft-label (logit) matching, feature- or attention-level imitation, multi-teacher fusion, data-free distillation, and adaptations for domain shift and heterogeneous deployment. Empirical results show distilled students can approach or match teacher performance in many settings, but success depends on teacher quality, the form of transferred knowledge, training curricula, and application-specific design choices. Emerging theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and reveal practical tradeoffs such as bias–variance effects of soft labels and the roles of ensemble and self-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Tool: Compression, Regularization, and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a compression heuristic into a versatile training paradigm that enables model size reduction, improved generalization, domain adaptation, and task consolidation. Its practical success depends on both the sources of teacher supervision (final logits, intermediate representations, or multiple teachers) and how distillation is applied (sample selection, layer matching, or label design). While KD frequently yields compact, high-performing models, its benefits arise from a mixture of transferred dark knowledge and regularizing effects of soft targets; careful design choices are required to realize those benefits across settings such as language model compression, multi-task training, and privacy-constrained or heterogeneous environments.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels—ranging from softened logits to intermediate representations and relational signals—KD enables substantial reductions in parameters and latency while preserving much of the teacher's performance. When combined with complementary compression tools and careful teacher–student co-design, distillation provides a practical first-line strategy for real-world model compression, though important open problems remain around fairness, data availability, heterogeneity, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and distributed settings KD often recovers much of a teacher's predictive performance while enabling faster inference, lower memory use, and deployment under resource or privacy constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: outcomes depend on what signals are transferred (logits, features, attention), teacher–student compatibility, availability and quality of data (including data-free or federated setups), and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Best practice treats distillation as one element of a compression pipeline that combines representation matching, architecture-aware student design, data strategies, and risk-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are a widely adopted toolkit for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the accuracy of larger teachers. Research across vision and language characterizes KD as a family of methods—transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training signals via specialized curricula or online exchanges—and shows that KD integrates naturally with pretraining, architecture design, and deployment-aware strategies. Practical success depends on matching the choice of knowledge (what to transfer), the teacher-student pairing (capacity and architecture), available data (real, augmented, or synthetic), and optimization curricula to the target task and constraints. While KD routinely yields substantial runtime and memory gains with modest accuracy loss, open challenges remain in handling domain shift, rare-token transfer in NLP, optimization mismatch, and large-scale or privacy-sensitive deployments.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels—soft logits, intermediate representations, attention patterns, and relational signals—to enable substantial reductions in size and latency while preserving much teacher performance. Its success in practice depends on careful choice of distillation targets, teacher–student compatibility, data strategies (including synthetic or data-free approaches), and complementary compression methods. KD is powerful but not universal: optimization mismatch, domain shift, and limited data can undermine transfer, so robust pipelines co-design student architectures, distillation signals, and training/data workflows to realize production gains.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other forms of teacher knowledge. Across vision and language tasks KD has enabled practical reductions in model size and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance. Success depends on what form of knowledge is transferred, how teacher and student representations are aligned, the availability and selection of data for distillation, and complementary compression techniques such as low-precision numerics, pruning, or architecture adaptation. Remaining challenges include optimization barriers that prevent exact teacher matching, reliable distillation without original data, robustness and fairness under compression, and principled methods for matching heterogeneous teacher–student pairs.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broad, practical toolkit for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers across vision, language, generative, and multimodal domains. Research shows KD can preserve—and in some settings improve—task performance while enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency when combined with complementary strategies. Practical success depends on what is transferred (outputs, internal features, attention), how teacher and student are aligned architecturally and procedurally, and on data and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used and flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teacher models. Over the past decade KD has grown from matching softened output distributions to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, data-free/zero-shot synthesis, and architecture-aware co-design. Empirical work demonstrates KD's ability to reduce parameter counts and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance across vision, speech, and language tasks; its practical success depends on careful choices of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to manage data and augmentation. Remaining challenges include robust distillation under domain shift, preserving rare-token behavior in language models, privacy-sensitive settings, and principled combination of KD with other compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster ones while preserving performance, enabling deployment under resource, latency, privacy, and domain-specific constraints. Across modalities and tasks, KD can be combined with architectural search, feature-level objectives, teacher optimization, and data-free methods to meet diverse production requirements. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a primary instrument in model-compression toolkits for modern deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, Applications, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s capability. KD encompasses matching teacher soft targets, transferring intermediate representations or attentions, leveraging ensembles or self-teaching, and operating in constrained settings via data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Across vision, generative models, and natural language tasks, distillation is used both as a standalone compression technique and as a complement to pruning and quantization. Success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability, and how to mitigate optimization and distributional mismatches. While KD often produces compact models that approach teacher performance, practical deployment requires careful design to avoid failure modes arising from heterogeneous data, limited student capacity, or misaligned training objectives.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features/attention, relational or structural signals) and can be applied in offline, online, ensemble, or data-constrained settings. Empirical results across vision, speech, and language show that appropriately designed distillation pipelines can deliver large efficiency gains with modest loss (and sometimes gains) in accuracy, but success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, data availability, and deployment constraints. Practical deployments typically combine KD with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and require design attention to robustness, domain shift, and privacy.
