papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First-line, Context-aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to what knowledge is transferred, how intermediate layers are aligned, and whether data or privacy constraints hold, KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance while enabling large gains in inference speed and memory. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: optimization difficulties, mismatches in capacity between teacher and student, and limited or private data require tailored objectives, architecture-aware choices, and complementary techniques. This essay argues KD should be a primary strategy in model-compression toolkits while recommending concrete practices to increase reliability across real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multi‑Strategy, Practical — but Bounded — Path for Compressing Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. When applied thoughtfully — combining soft-label transfer with representation-level guidance, architecture-aware design, and data strategies — KD enables compact models that meet memory, latency, and deployment constraints while retaining most of a teacher’s performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: limited or private data, teacher errors, student capacity gaps, and robustness or fairness concerns create concrete failure modes that require complementary methods and careful evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a multi-strategy engineering approach whose best results arise from combining several targeted techniques that suit task, data, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for producing compact models that meet deployment constraints in compute, memory, latency, and privacy. When integrated with complementary techniques (layer mapping, data strategies, adversarial training, and architecture-aware design), KD enables substantial compression with modest performance loss across vision and language tasks. Realizing these gains requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data. This paper argues that KD should be a first-line strategy in compression pipelines while outlining practical caveats and design recommendations for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have become central tools for deploying deep models in constrained environments. Work in this area spans simple teacher–student soft-label transfer to advanced feature- and layer-level matching, adversarial and data-free approaches, and automated search guided by distillation. Applications include compressing pre-trained language models, accelerating non-autoregressive translation, compressing generative models, and improving low-precision inference. Empirical and theoretical studies highlight both practical recipes (mixing hard and soft labels, many-to-many layer mappings, feature mimicking) and conceptual explanations (connections to label smoothing and regularization), while open challenges remain in retaining rare-token behavior, mitigating bias transfer, and scaling distillation to privacy- or data-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Methods, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or aggregated multi-teacher signals—KD enables compact models that retain much of teacher performance while supporting complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware changes). KD also adapts to constrained settings (limited or private data, domain-specialization, federated or black-box teachers) but requires careful design choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and training curricula. When applied as part of a principled compression pipeline, KD offers a practical route to deployable high-quality models, though open problems remain in preserving rare-token behaviors, robustness, and reliable operation under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and broadly applicable technique to compress large neural models into smaller, faster models while preserving much of their performance. Work across computer vision, speech, and natural language processing demonstrates that KD can enable deployment of resource-efficient models, improve generalization in constrained settings, and be combined with other compression methods (e.g., low-precision numerics). At the same time, the field has identified important limitations and nuanced behaviors — such as data simplification effects, teacher–student mismatches, and domain or task-specific failure modes — that guide how KD should be applied in practice. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, variants, empirical benefits, and practical considerations for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Practical Case for Richer Knowledge Distillation in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a necessary and practical tool for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings, but its value depends critically on what is distilled and how. Soft-label matching transfers useful "dark knowledge" from ensembles, yet by itself often fails to capture internal structure, handle domain or data heterogeneity, or operate when original data are unavailable. Combining soft labels with internal- and feature-level guidance, architecture- and task-aware compression, and data- or privacy-aware generation strategies yields more robust, compact models that retain teacher performance across NLP and broader deep learning tasks.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Theory, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach to compress large deep models and transfer knowledge to smaller, faster, or more interpretable models. Across vision and language applications, KD encompasses teacher-student paradigms that use teacher soft targets, intermediate representations, or auxiliary objectives; extensions include multi-teacher setups, data-free distillation, meta-learned teachers, and device-aware distillation for heterogeneous deployments. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude reductions in parameters and inference cost; theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and how dataset complexity, teacher quality, and student capacity interact to determine outcomes. Practical strategies combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware techniques to meet deployment constraints while retaining generalization.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Dependent Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable route to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their predictive capability. KD achieves favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across modalities and tasks, but its real-world success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and deployment constraints. A pragmatic approach treats KD as a core tool that should routinely be combined with complementary compression, data, and training strategies.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a General-Purpose Compression Strategy for Deep Models: Evidence, Mechanisms, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a specialized technique for transferring softened output distributions into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing and adapting deep models across domains (vision, language, multimodal, and generative models). Empirical results across tasks show that KD can preserve or even improve accuracy while substantially reducing model size and latency, and it can be combined with complementary strategies (pre-training, low-precision arithmetic, data synthesis, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints and privacy requirements. However, effective distillation requires attention to what is transferred (logits, internal representations, attention maps), how teachers and students are aligned (layer mapping, input alignment), and whether real data are available (data-free or adversarially guided generation). This paper synthesizes evidence from recent work to argue that KD, when applied with these considerations, is a reliable foundation for practical model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: Toward Representation- and Strategy-driven Knowledge Distillation for Efficient and Robust NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation remains a central approach to compress large deep learning models for deployment in resource-constrained and domain-specific NLP settings. I argue that to realize reliably compact and generalizable student models we must move past sole reliance on teacher soft-labels and adopt representation-aware objectives, structured channel/feature matching, adaptive training curricula, and practical strategies for low-precision, data-limited, and privacy-sensitive scenarios. Combining these approaches yields students that better capture teacher knowledge, adapt to new domains, and meet real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a predominant strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. Across vision, language, speech, and other modalities, KD encompasses soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention imitation, relational and training-dynamics transfer, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. When integrated with architecture-level compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful teacher–student co-design, KD enables substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss and can sometimes improve robustness or generalization. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align layers and representations, data availability, and safeguards for fairness and privacy; these constitute active areas of empirical and methodological work.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other forms of teacher knowledge. Across vision and language tasks KD has enabled practical reductions in model size and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance. Success depends on what form of knowledge is transferred, how teacher and student representations are aligned, the availability and selection of data for distillation, and complementary compression techniques such as low-precision numerics, pruning, or architecture adaptation. Remaining challenges include optimization barriers that prevent exact teacher matching, reliable distillation without original data, robustness and fairness under compression, and principled methods for matching heterogeneous teacher–student pairs.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: The Versatility and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students while preserving much of their performance. Across domains — including reinforcement learning, vision, generative modeling, and language — distillation can accelerate inference, enable deployment on constrained devices, and transfer capabilities such as domain adaptation or lifelong learning. However, its effectiveness depends on choices about teacher-student pairing, data availability and augmentation, sample selection, and training protocols; it also interacts with privacy and heterogeneity constraints. A balanced approach that combines principled distillation objectives, appropriate data strategies (including data-free methods when necessary), and curriculum or annealing schedules yields the best tradeoffs between compactness and retained performance.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Compact, Robust Deep Models: Effectiveness, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD succeeds when its design (what to transfer, how, and with which data) is matched to deployment constraints: transferring logits, intermediate representations, or relational signals; using multi- or adaptive-teacher schedules; and combining distillation with model- and data-level compression. However, KD is not a panacea — optimization gaps, mismatched inputs or teachers, and inappropriate sample selection can degrade results — so robust application requires careful teacher-student co-design, selective supervision, and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multi‑Strategy Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to compressing large models into smaller, efficient students. When treated as a toolbox of complementary methods—logit-level supervision, representation matching, layer alignment, multi-teacher schedules, data synthesis, and privacy-aware mechanisms—KD enables compact models to approach the performance of larger teachers while meeting real-world constraints on latency, memory, and data access. At the same time, distillation outcomes depend on teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and optimization choices; addressing these limits requires careful method selection and integration with complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Versatile, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD has proven effective across modalities and tasks, enabling multimodal generation, compact evaluation metrics, and efficient inference. However, KD is not a black-box cure: its success depends on what is transferred (logits, features, intermediate layers), how teachers and students are paired or trained, and on optimization and regularization choices. I argue that KD should be viewed as a flexible toolkit—comprising feature-level mimicking, layer-aware projection, self- and teacher-free variants, and teacher-adaptation strategies—applied with careful attention to teacher-student interaction and training dynamics to achieve reliable compression in practice.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central family of techniques for compressing and accelerating deep models by transferring information from larger (teacher) models or training dynamics into smaller (student) models. Across domains and modalities—vision, graph data, speech, and natural language—KD variants address different constraints: limited data or privacy, distributed training, domain shift, and task-specific requirements (e.g., ranking, generation, or sequence modeling). Mechanistically, KD leverages richer supervisory signals than hard labels (soft targets, intermediate features, relational structure, or training trajectories) to regularize students and often yields students that approach teacher accuracy while improving latency and memory. Recent work has clarified connections between KD and other regularizers (e.g., label smoothing), introduced teacher-free and self-distillation approaches, explored the role of data augmentation and feature projectors, and adapted KD to federated, ensemble, and cross-task settings. Empirical results across tasks show KD can enable large compression/acceleration gains with modest performance loss and, in some settings, even improve generalization and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models to reduce inference cost while attempting to preserve predictive performance. KD encompasses a range of mechanisms — soft-target (logit) matching, feature and intermediate-layer imitation, attention- or channel-based guidance, ensemble-to-single-model transfer, self-distillation, and data- or device-aware variants — and is applied across modalities including vision and language. Empirical work shows KD can yield substantial reductions in parameters and latency with modest accuracy loss, and in some settings can improve student generalization. Practical deployment couples KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and requires careful design choices around teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific objectives.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a simple teacher-student training recipe into a multifaceted toolkit that enables efficient, robust, and privacy-aware deployment of deep models. KD not only compresses large models into faster, smaller students suitable for edge and production, but also enables task-adaptive compression, data-limited or data-free scenarios, privacy-preserving federated setups, and transfers of inductive biases across architectures. When combined with complementary techniques such as architecture search, specialized feature-matching losses, and careful input-side interventions, KD yields practical compressed models without prohibitive losses in accuracy and can improve generalization in out-of-distribution settings.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a primary, practical strategy for compressing large deep models into small, deployable students across vision and language tasks. KD is flexible: it supports soft-target transfer, intermediate representation matching, attention-guided feature matching, multi-teacher ensembles, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When combined with architecture-aware design, low-precision numerics, and data synthesis or augmentation, KD produces compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. However, effective deployment requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to mitigate risks such as transferred biases, robustness loss, and teacher–student mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential and Practical, but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance while reducing parameter count and inference cost, but its reliability depends on choices about what to distill, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited, heterogeneous, or private data. Realistic deployment requires combining KD with complementary compression techniques, adapting the distillation signal to the task and student capacity, and evaluating robustness and privacy implications.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System-level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, versatile approach for shrinking large models into compact students that are deployable under compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints. Its success depends on treating distillation not as a single loss but as a system design choice: selecting what signals to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relations), how to align teacher and student architectures and capacities, what data or synthetic surrogates to use, and which complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) to combine. KD delivers substantial efficiency gains in many settings but is context-dependent: careful choices about teacher quality, data availability, and objective design are required to avoid failure modes such as capacity mismatch, degraded handling of low-frequency phenomena, or privacy/robustness tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A spectrum of distillation signals—soft logits, intermediate features and attention, relational/contrastive objectives, multi-teacher ensembles, and data- or privacy-aware synthesis—enables compact models that often retain most of teacher performance. Empirical results across NLP, speech, graph learning, and vision show KD’s practical value, while theoretical and empirical analyses point to mechanisms (soft-target regularization, ensemble-induced ‘‘dark knowledge’’, and representation shaping) and to limits tied to student capacity, data alignment, optimization dynamics, and robustness under distribution shift. Practical deployment requires careful selection of what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design).

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation: Task-adaptive, Privacy-aware, and Feature-centric Compression for Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are now essential tools to deploy large deep models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. When applied thoughtfully—adapting to task requirements, leveraging feature-level signals, and accounting for data availability—KD can yield compact models that retain much of the teacher's performance while improving inference speed, memory footprint, and interpretability. However, naive distillation can fail under data heterogeneity, limited data, or strong teacher–student mismatches; addressing these requires task-aware layer selection, multi-teacher strategies, and alternatives to standard logit matching. I argue that the most effective KD pipelines combine task-adaptive compression, feature-directed supervision, and methods that preserve privacy and robustness to limited data.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models so they can be deployed under memory, latency, or privacy constraints. Across computer vision, speech, and natural language processing, KD has evolved from matching teacher logits to a broad set of practices that include intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher schedules, data-free or black-box distillation, and architecture-aware compression. These methods routinely yield substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but success depends on choices about the type of knowledge transferred, the student initialization and capacity, the availability and provenance of data, and evaluation for robustness and undesired behavior.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to reproduce useful behavior of larger teacher models so that deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints becomes practical. KD encompasses a family of techniques — from matching teacher output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure — and is commonly combined with complementary compressions such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows that, when matched to student capacity and data availability, distilled students can approach teacher performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. Practical success depends on choices about which signals to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data access (including data-free alternatives), and robustness or fairness requirements; remaining challenges concern principled objective design, optimization under capacity mismatch, and reliable transfer of robustness and rare-token/long-tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unifying Tool: Compression, Transfer, and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) began as a model compression technique but has evolved into a flexible framework that accomplishes compression, regularization, domain adaptation, continual learning, fairness mitigation, and inductive-bias transfer across architectures and modalities. By choosing what to transfer (logits, features, relations, or module behavior) and how to weight multi-source supervision, practitioners can adapt KD to the constraints and objectives of specific tasks. This paper argues that KD should be treated not merely as a compression trick but as a general-purpose mechanism for shaping student models, and it synthesizes empirical and theoretical evidence to recommend practical best practices for applying KD across modern deep learning and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Powerful, Multifaceted, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and versatile approach for compressing deep models for deployment in constrained environments. KD methods transfer predictive behavior and internal information from larger teachers to smaller students using a range of targets and training regimes; when combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression steps, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, latency, and compute while retaining much of teacher performance. However, the method’s effectiveness depends on careful selection of transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and mitigation of undesirable teacher behavior, so KD should be applied as part of an integrated compression strategy rather than a single silver-bullet solution.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When combined with representation-level objectives, architecture-aware techniques, and deployment-aware protocols, KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling real-world constraints such as latency, memory, and device heterogeneity to be met. Best practices include selecting appropriate distilled signals (beyond soft labels), pretraining or warming students, and aligning objectives with deployment constraints. Despite strong empirical success across modalities, open challenges remain in handling data heterogeneity, domain shift, privacy-sensitive settings, and the automated design of student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Methods, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or aggregated multi-teacher signals—KD enables compact models that retain much of teacher performance while supporting complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware changes). KD also adapts to constrained settings (limited or private data, domain-specialization, federated or black-box teachers) but requires careful design choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and training curricula. When applied as part of a principled compression pipeline, KD offers a practical route to deployable high-quality models, though open problems remain in preserving rare-token behaviors, robustness, and reliable operation under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: The Practical Foundations and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their accuracy. Its success arises from multiple complementary mechanisms—soft-target regularization, internal representation transfer, and architectural or data-side adaptations—that together explain why KD works across modalities (vision, language, graphs) and tasks (classification, QA, generation). However, KD is not a silver bullet: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality and compatibility, data properties (including augmentation and low-frequency phenomena), and deployment constraints such as federated or heterogeneous environments. Recognizing these mechanisms and limitations enables principled choices (e.g., teacher design, feature/projector choices, multi-teacher or adversarial schemes, and data strategies) to get the best trade-offs between compression and performance.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to emulate larger teacher models so deployments meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD encompasses a spectrum of signals to transfer—including softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure—and integrates with pruning, quantization, and architecture design to produce efficient models. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often preserves large portions of teacher performance and can improve student generalization beyond mere compression, but outcomes depend strongly on what is distilled, teacher–student compatibility, access to data, and optimization choices. Practical pipelines therefore combine signal design, data strategies, and task-aware architecture choices to balance efficiency, robustness, and retained performance; open problems remain in data-free and privacy-preserving distillation, principled teacher design, and reliably transferring robustness and rare-token fidelity in sequence tasks.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to emulate larger teacher models so that inference cost, memory, and latency are reduced while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and channel-wise transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. KD is most effective when matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints and is typically combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) to meet practical requirements. Important limits remain — including sensitivity to teacher-student mismatch, domain shift, robustness and fairness concerns, and data scarcity — motivating hybrid methods and careful evaluation in applied settings.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses or transfers knowledge from larger, more expensive models (teachers) into smaller, cheaper models (students) by using richer supervision than hard labels alone. The literature has developed multiple complementary strategies—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, architecturally guided replacement, multi-teacher schedules, data- and privacy-aware variants, and teacher-training schemes—to address deployment constraints, domain shift, and limited or private data. Empirical work shows these approaches can close much of the performance gap to full-size models across classification, language understanding, and retrieval tasks; theoretical and empirical analyses explain why distillation often improves generalization beyond mere compression. Remaining challenges include input distribution mismatch, low-frequency token fidelity in sequence tasks, and robust distillation without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Rasmussen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with task-aware choices for what and how to transfer (soft labels, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), and when combined with complementary compression strategies (architecture adaptation, pruning, quantization, data augmentation or synthesis), KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student alignment, availability or synthesis of appropriate data, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy risks. Practical compression pipelines therefore treat distillation as a core tool whose design must be tailored to the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First-Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Power, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of techniques for converting large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When combined with complementary strategies—pre-training compact architectures, feature-level supervision, multi-teacher schedules, data synthesis or augmentation, and task-aware student design—KD yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks. However, realizing those gains in practice requires attention to teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, choice of distilled signals, and data availability; without such care, distillation can underperform or lose task-specific signals. I argue KD should be the first-line approach for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP pipelines, provided practitioners adopt principled, context-aware distillation recipes.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single logit-matching trick into a versatile, task- and deployment-aware toolkit that can produce compact models with strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. By transferring soft targets, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and by integrating with architecture search, data augmentation, and heterogeneous-teacher setups, KD enables practical compression across vision and language modalities. This paper argues KD should be a first-line technique for model compression in deep learning and NLP, describes the complementary methods that make it effective in production settings, and highlights common pitfalls and practical remedies for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Bounded Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-strategy approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods include transferring softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and data-free or few-shot variants to handle limited or private data. Best results come from treating KD as one element of a broader compression pipeline that also incorporates architecture-aware choices, data strategies, and explicit attention to robustness and fairness. KD is therefore a central tool for efficient deployment, but it has clear limits and must be designed carefully to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors or losing rare-token performance.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features/attention, relational or structural signals) and can be applied in offline, online, ensemble, or data-constrained settings. Empirical results across vision, speech, and language show that appropriately designed distillation pipelines can deliver large efficiency gains with modest loss (and sometimes gains) in accuracy, but success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, data availability, and deployment constraints. Practical deployments typically combine KD with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and require design attention to robustness, domain shift, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Compressing and Deploying Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible technique that enables transferring predictive power from large models into smaller or more efficient ones. When combined with complementary strategies such as pre-training of compact architectures, task-aware selection of distilled signals, quantization-aware training, and privacy-preserving or federated protocols, KD can make state-of-the-art models practically usable on resource-constrained and heterogeneous devices. However, realizing these gains requires attention to what is distilled (outputs versus internal representations), how distilled signals are selected for the target task, and whether data-privacy or communication constraints demand synthetic or distributed distillation procedures.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Aware Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of the teachers' predictive power. When combined with representation matching, architecture-aware alignment, pre-training of compact models, and appropriate data strategies, KD reliably improves inference efficiency while preserving accuracy in many vision and language tasks. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: it requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or heterogeneous data and fairness constraints. Pragmatic deployment therefore treats KD as a first‑line method that must be adapted to task, data, and resource constraints rather than a one‑size‑fits‑all recipe.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Pragmatic Design Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable family of methods that enables deployment of high-performing but resource-hungry models by training compact students that retain much of teacher behavior. KD delivers major operational benefits — reduced inference latency, lower memory footprint, and greater deployability under compute, bandwidth, and privacy constraints — but it is not a one-size-fits-all cure. Real-world success requires treating KD as a design paradigm: choose what form of knowledge to transfer (soft targets, intermediate features, relations), co-design teacher and student capacities, address data limitations (via targeted augmentation or synthetic data), and explicitly manage robustness, fairness, and rare-token behaviors. When combined with complementary compression tools and careful evaluation, KD is the central practical strategy for producing efficient, reliable models for modern NLP and deep-learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.
