papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile approach to compress large neural models for deployment, while preserving performance and enabling new capabilities such as efficient federated learning, data-free compression, interpretability, and few-shot adaptation. Across architectures and tasks, KD variants—ranging from layer-to-layer alignment and progressive module replacement to meta-learned teachers and adversarial data synthesis—provide methods to trade computation, memory, and communication for small changes in accuracy. These methods make it possible to bring large pretrained models into production and edge settings, and to reconcile competing requirements such as privacy, heterogeneity, and interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression are indispensable tools to deploy high-performing deep models under compute, memory, privacy, and latency constraints. Across modalities and tasks, effective compression requires more than copying teacher logits: practitioners should match richer internal representations, align inputs and tokenization across teacher and student, design teacher updates that explicitly optimize transfer, and account for privacy and robustness needs. When applied thoughtfully, KD can produce compact models that retain much of the teacher’s utility and in some cases improve efficiency beyond the original models.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Multi-purpose Strategy for Model Compression and Robust Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving or even improving task performance. Beyond simple size reduction, KD supports domain adaptation, latency-aware architecture transformations, robustness transfer, and interpretable model surrogates. When combined with careful training protocols (e.g., multi-teacher schemes, domain adaptation, or targeted regularization), distillation enables deployment of high-performing models in resource- and latency-constrained or safety-critical settings across vision, speech, 3D perception, and natural language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When combined with representation-level objectives, architecture-aware techniques, and deployment-aware protocols, KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling real-world constraints such as latency, memory, and device heterogeneity to be met. Best practices include selecting appropriate distilled signals (beyond soft labels), pretraining or warming students, and aligning objectives with deployment constraints. Despite strong empirical success across modalities, open challenges remain in handling data heterogeneity, domain shift, privacy-sensitive settings, and the automated design of student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multi‑Strategy Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to compressing large models into smaller, efficient students. When treated as a toolbox of complementary methods—logit-level supervision, representation matching, layer alignment, multi-teacher schedules, data synthesis, and privacy-aware mechanisms—KD enables compact models to approach the performance of larger teachers while meeting real-world constraints on latency, memory, and data access. At the same time, distillation outcomes depend on teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and optimization choices; addressing these limits requires careful method selection and integration with complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD transfers information beyond hard labels — including softened output distributions, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational signals — and is commonly combined with architectural or numerical compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD can yield large efficiency gains with modest performance loss when teacher–student design, data availability, and optimization dynamics are considered; however, its success is contingent on capacity alignment, data choices, and safeguards against transferring undesirable behaviors. Applications range from accelerated inference and edge deployment to domain adaptation, federated learning, and task-specific adaptations such as non-autoregressive translation and graph-to-MLP compression.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to emulate larger teacher models so that inference cost, memory, and latency are reduced while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and channel-wise transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. KD is most effective when matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints and is typically combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) to meet practical requirements. Important limits remain — including sensitivity to teacher-student mismatch, domain shift, robustness and fairness concerns, and data scarcity — motivating hybrid methods and careful evaluation in applied settings.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural networks into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher(s) to student(s). Advances span logit- and feature-based matching, multi-teacher and curriculum strategies, data-free and federated scenarios, and domain- or task-specific adaptations in NLP. Practical work shows KD can yield large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but design choices (what to match, how to weight teachers, whether data are available, and deployment constraints) strongly affect outcomes. Remaining challenges include robustness to domain shift, privacy and communication constraints in distributed settings, and principled handling of teacher–student mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transform large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, faster, and more deployable models while attempting to preserve accuracy and useful inductive biases. Approaches span classic teacher–student logit matching, representation and feature imitation, layer mapping strategies for large pretrained language models, data-free and zero-shot methods that avoid access to original training data, and privacy- or communication-aware frameworks for distributed settings. Empirical work demonstrates these methods can yield practical speedups, substantial parameter reductions, and competitive task performance across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks; theoretical and empirical studies also clarify when softened teacher targets or distilled datasets best help student capacity. Remaining challenges include balancing privacy and utility, reducing the cost of distillation when teachers are large, and extending guarantees and methods across modalities and domain shifts.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer information from larger, more expensive models (teachers) into smaller, cheaper models (students) to reduce inference cost, enable deployment in constrained environments, or impart desirable properties such as robustness or interpretability. Across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks, researchers have developed a spectrum of KD strategies — from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate features, attention, or relational signals — and combined these with architecture-level compression, pretraining, and data-management strategies. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often approach teacher performance, but success depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation target, data availability, and training dynamics. Open problems include reliable distillation without original data, transferring inductive biases and robustness, and handling heterogeneous or federated data and models.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring useful predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, KD variants—ranging from soft-target matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware approaches—enable substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher and student design, data and augmentation strategies, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, low-precision numerics). When these components are co-designed, distilled models can approach teacher-level performance and support real-world, resource-constrained deployments, though open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, rare-token fidelity, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable method for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD succeeds when its objectives, representation targets, and training regimes are chosen to match deployment constraints and student capacity; combining KD with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, data-free synthesis, and online protocols) extends its reach. However, KD also transfers risks (bias, privacy leakage, fragility) and faces limits when teacher signals are mismatched or training data are scarce, motivating task-aware design, robust distillation objectives, and emergent meta- and data-free methods.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Effective Practices for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques reliably reduce large pretrained models to compact, efficient students suitable for deployment while preserving most of the teacher performance. Across NLP and multimodal tasks, practical compression requires strategies that (1) align representations at multiple levels, (2) focus on task-relevant information, and (3) handle limited or no access to original training data. Combining architecture-aware search, progressive module replacement, task-aware layer selection, and improved input-side strategies (including data augmentation or data-free sample generation) yields compact models with strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs suitable for real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Best Practices and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Efficient Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a foundational technique for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the accuracy of larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and graph domains. When applied thoughtfully — combining representational objectives, teacher-student co-design, task-aware compression, and appropriate data strategies — KD enables deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining robustness and fairness. However, pitfalls arise from mismatches in inputs, teacher strength, data availability, and dataset biases; practical KD should therefore be integrated with complementary methods (e.g., architecture search, pruning, curriculum strategies, and data-generation) and with safeguards for ethical concerns.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Powerful, Multifaceted, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and versatile approach for compressing deep models for deployment in constrained environments. KD methods transfer predictive behavior and internal information from larger teachers to smaller students using a range of targets and training regimes; when combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression steps, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, latency, and compute while retaining much of teacher performance. However, the method’s effectiveness depends on careful selection of transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and mitigation of undesirable teacher behavior, so KD should be applied as part of an integrated compression strategy rather than a single silver-bullet solution.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Dependent Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable route to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their predictive capability. KD achieves favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across modalities and tasks, but its real-world success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and deployment constraints. A pragmatic approach treats KD as a core tool that should routinely be combined with complementary compression, data, and training strategies.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Concise Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of teacher performance. Research across vision, speech, translation, and NLP tasks has developed multiple KD objectives (soft logits, intermediate-feature matching, attention or projector-based alignment), training regimes (offline teacher–student, self-distillation, multi-teacher, adversarial transfer), and data strategies (data-free, distilled datasets, and hybrid authentic/synthetic training). Empirical and theoretical work explains why KD often improves student generalization (dark-knowledge regularization, transferred inductive biases) while also documenting limitations (capacity mismatch, teacher error propagation, distributional/low-frequency failures) and practical remedies. Best practice is to treat KD as a flexible toolkit and combine it with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. The field comprises a family of methods that transfer different forms of information—from soft logits to internal representations, attention maps, and relational structure—and integrates naturally with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Success depends on choosing what to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacities and architectures, managing data availability (including data-free or federated setups), and designing appropriate optimization curricula. While KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, important limitations remain around teacher–student mismatch, domain shift, rare-token preservation in NLP, and robustness under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Representation-aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolbox—combining soft-target supervision, intermediate representation matching, attention- or layer-aware mappings, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-conscious strategies—KD yields compact models that better preserve teacher behavior while meeting deployment constraints. However, realizing those benefits requires attention to teacher–student compatibility, choice of distilled signals, and data constraints; KD is powerful but not a universal remedy.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The approach spans logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, self-distillation, multi-teacher and data-free variants, and combinations with structural compression such as pruning and quantization. KD is effective across modalities and tasks but its empirical success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and training dynamics; open challenges remain in preserving rare-token behavior, robustness, privacy, and heterogeneous architecture transfer.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and widely applicable approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks—language understanding, retrieval, visual recognition, graph-based prediction, and data-limited or privacy-constrained settings—distillation enables latency- and resource-constrained deployment. However, straightforward distillation is not a panacea: distribution shifts, heterogeneity of data and models, and absence of training data expose weaknesses that require complementary techniques (e.g., internal representation matching, layer mapping, task-aware selection, generative replay). Combining these advances yields compressed models that are both accurate and robust for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from larger, richer teacher models to smaller, cheaper student models to enable deployment under compute, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature encompasses simple soft-label matching, richer supervision signals that align intermediate features or attention, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-preserving designs, and combinations with structural compression such as pruning and layer skipping. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation can both compress and regularize models, but effectiveness depends on teacher-student mismatch, data availability, and optimization choices; practical pipelines therefore combine multiple compression mechanisms, careful signal selection, and task-aware adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring useful information from teacher models. Across vision, speech, reinforcement learning, and NLP, KD has been adapted into logit-level supervision, intermediate feature and layer-wise matching, data augmentation strategies, data-free setups, and training-time architectural replacement. Recent work has expanded KD to address practical constraints—privacy in federated settings, bias mitigation in language models, low-precision deployment, and multi-task transfer—while also proposing task-aware and capacity-aware methods to reduce redundant or harmful teacher signals. This synthesis summarizes the mechanisms, extensions, strengths, and limitations documented in contemporary studies and highlights promising directions for making distilled models both efficient and robust.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Effective, Multifaceted, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their performance. KD operates via multiple knowledge channels — softened logits, intermediate feature matching, attention or relational signals, and ensemble or multi-teacher supervision — and it composes well with other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architectural replacement). Empirical results across vision, speech, and NLP show that carefully chosen distillation targets, student pre-training, data augmentation, and multi-teacher strategies reliably improve deployment trade-offs, but KD’s success depends on data availability, teacher–student alignment, and domain heterogeneity. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a flexible pipeline: design the student and distillation targets for the task and capacity of the student, use multi-source or ensemble teachers when appropriate, apply representation projection to reconcile mismatches, and explicitly evaluate under realistic data heterogeneity or deployment constraints to avoid hidden failures.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, distillation methods—ranging from matching teacher soft targets to aligning intermediate features or using data-free synthesis—enable substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical deployments combine distillation with architecture-aware choices (pruning, replacement, or search), multi-teacher or online schemes, and task-aware data strategies. Success depends on teacher quality, choice of transfer targets, data availability, and handling of mismatches; when carefully designed, distillation yields compact, robust models suitable for resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: The Strengths and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large models into deployable, efficient students across modalities. Empirical work shows KD can preserve task performance while drastically reducing size and compute, but its success depends on choices of what and how to transfer, availability and provenance of data, and training dynamics. Advances in feature-matching, progressive module replacement, task-aware layer selection, data-free synthesis, and robustness-aware distillation expand KD's applicability but do not eliminate core challenges—optimization barriers, distribution heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and potential transfer of unwanted behaviors. A careful, task-aware combination of techniques is therefore required to realize reliable, compact models for production use.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses information from larger, often more expensive teacher models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Research over the past decade has developed a spectrum of KD objectives (soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention alignment, contrastive and relational losses), training regimes (offline teacher-student, online co-training, self-distillation, multi-teacher schedules), and deployment-aware integrations (pre-training students, architecture-aware adapters, and combination with pruning or quantization). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance while reducing parameter count and latency, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and the choice of what and how to transfer. Ongoing challenges include robust transfer under distribution shift, matching heterogeneous architectures, preserving low-frequency or domain-specific signals, and automating trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, Applications, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s capability. KD encompasses matching teacher soft targets, transferring intermediate representations or attentions, leveraging ensembles or self-teaching, and operating in constrained settings via data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Across vision, generative models, and natural language tasks, distillation is used both as a standalone compression technique and as a complement to pruning and quantization. Success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability, and how to mitigate optimization and distributional mismatches. While KD often produces compact models that approach teacher performance, practical deployment requires careful design to avoid failure modes arising from heterogeneous data, limited student capacity, or misaligned training objectives.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques that transfer information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive signals), how data are used or synthesized, and how training is scheduled (offline, online, self-distillation, adversarial compression). Empirical work shows KD can enable deployable models across vision, speech, and NLP, but success depends on aligning teacher-student inputs and representations, addressing optimization mismatches, and adapting objectives to task and data constraints. Open challenges include data-free distillation, cross-domain generalization, robustness, fairness, and principled choices of distillation targets for heterogeneous student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transform large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, faster, and more deployable models. Across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks, methods include soft-target (logit) distillation, feature and representation matching, layer-mapping strategies for large pretrained models, data- and privacy-aware protocols, and training-time variants such as online or co-distillation. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often retain much of teacher performance while yielding substantial savings in memory, latency, and energy; however, outcomes depend on teacher–student compatibility, access to task data, which signals are transferred, and training protocol choices. Key open problems include robust cross-domain transfer, handling teacher errors and low-frequency phenomena, and reducing distillation cost when teachers are large or data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Open Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, cheaper students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, methods range from classic teacher-student logits supervision to data-free and online schemes, meta-learned teachers, and representation-level transfers. Empirical work shows KD often yields substantial efficiency gains but its effectiveness depends on dataset complexity, model capacity, data availability, and optimization choices; important failure modes and practical remediation strategies have been identified.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: The Centrality of Knowledge Distillation in Modern Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational technique for compressing large neural models while retaining much of their performance. Across vision and language tasks, distillation can act both as a compression mechanism and as a regularizer, and it integrates naturally with complementary strategies such as architecture search, layer-wise alignment, representation matching, data augmentation, pruning, and deployment-aware methods. When applied thoughtfully—matching teacher and student representations, tuning the signal provided by soft labels, and adapting to task or device constraints—distillation enables practical, high-performing compressed models suitable for production and edge settings.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) uses larger or ensemble teacher models to train smaller student models that retain much of the teacher’s predictive ability while reducing inference cost. Over the past decade KD has expanded from matching softened outputs to include intermediate representation matching, layer- and channel-wise guidance, ensemble and multi-teacher approaches, self-distillation, data-free and federated variants, and integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work demonstrates substantial size and latency reductions across vision and NLP with modest accuracy loss when methods are carefully chosen and paired with appropriate data or synthesis strategies. Remaining practical and scientific challenges include robust cross-domain transfer, operating without original training data, mitigating transferred biases, and aligning heterogeneous teacher–student capacities.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones in deep learning and NLP. Treated as a flexible toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of a teacher’s performance when its objectives, targets, and training strategies are matched to deployment constraints and student capacity. Effective application requires combining KD variants with complementary compression techniques and careful evaluation of robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. Across vision and language tasks, KD has been adapted beyond simple soft-label matching to include intermediate-feature supervision, layer- or module-level mapping, selective sample transfer, data-free synthesis, and combinations with other compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical deployments reveal important dependencies on teacher quality, student architecture, data availability, and training protocols; when these are handled deliberately, distilled models can achieve strong trade-offs in accuracy, latency, and resource use. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data heterogeneity, preserving low-frequency or rare outputs, and aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures in privacy-sensitive or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression are indispensable tools to deploy high-performing deep models under compute, memory, privacy, and latency constraints. Across modalities and tasks, effective compression requires more than copying teacher logits: practitioners should match richer internal representations, align inputs and tokenization across teacher and student, design teacher updates that explicitly optimize transfer, and account for privacy and robustness needs. When applied thoughtfully, KD can produce compact models that retain much of the teacher’s utility and in some cases improve efficiency beyond the original models.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD’s strengths arise from its flexibility in what and how information is transferred (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention, or relational signals) and from its ability to combine with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data augmentation). When applied with attention to teacher–student alignment, distilled signals, and data constraints, KD reliably improves accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities. However, KD is not universally sufficient: success requires careful method selection, handling of distributional and data limitations, and, in some cases, adversarial or privacy-aware extensions.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD techniques span soft-label transfer, intermediate representation matching, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher and ensemble guidance, and adaptations for constrained or distributed settings. When combined with careful pretraining, representation-aware losses, selective sample strategies, and attention to privacy or robustness requirements, KD enables practical deployment of high-quality models on resource-limited devices and in federated environments.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Constraints, and Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models or otherwise reduce model size while retaining performance. Core approaches include matching teacher soft-targets, aligning intermediate representations (features, attention), and combining distillation with structural compression (pruning, quantization) or automated architecture design. Practical uses span on-device deployment, task-adaptive compression, lifelong and continual learning, robustness preservation, and privacy-aware or data-free scenarios. Success depends on what is transferred, teacher–student compatibility, data availability (or synthesis), and training protocols; addressing these factors via complementary strategies yields the best accuracy–efficiency trade-offs while exposing open challenges in robustness, fairness, and out-of-distribution generalization.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central to deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained settings. The literature spans theoretical analyses of when and why distillation helps, practical algorithms for distilling logits, representations, and attention, techniques that require no original data, and adaptations for domains such as NLP, machine translation, and distributed training. Empirical work has shown KD can both accelerate inference and enable smaller models to approach or even exceed teacher performance in some settings, while recent advances address domain adaptivity, robustness, and teacher–student co-design.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single loss term but as a system-level design primitive that is matched to data availability, deployment constraints, and student–teacher mismatch. When designers select what to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, or relational signals), how to expose the student to informative inputs (real, synthesized, or online peer predictions), and how to adapt protocols for distributed or privacy-sensitive settings, KD yields large practical gains in latency, memory, and deployability while controlling risks such as bias transfer or robustness loss. A deployment-aware KD practice leverages representation-aware objectives, data-free synthesis when training data are unavailable, adversarial or online schemes for richer alignment, and federated-distillation architectures for communication-efficient collaboration.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across NLP, speech, vision, and recommendation systems, KD reduces inference cost and memory, enables deployment on constrained devices, and can transfer specialized capabilities when paired with appropriate data and training choices. Its effectiveness depends on what is distilled (soft targets, intermediate features, relational signals), the availability and synthesis of training data, and teacher–student design; complementary compression tools and safeguards addressing bias, privacy, and distributional mismatch are often required for robust, real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students. When designed to match the right form of teacher knowledge (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational or contrastive signals) and combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data provenance, and targeted objectives; therefore KD should be treated as a first-line tool that must be adapted to the deployment context rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from a single-teacher trick into a versatile family of methods that enable deployable, compact models across vision and language tasks. Empirical work across domains shows that distillation benefits from adopting strategies that reflect (1) where the student starts (pre-training), (2) what signals it receives (single, multi- or ensemble teachers; feature- and layer-level targets), and (3) the constraints of the deployment context (limited or no access to real data, heterogenous devices, or federated settings). Combining these insights yields practical recipes that reliably close the gap between large models and resource-constrained students while preserving robustness and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to mimic larger teacher models so that deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints becomes feasible. KD methods transfer different forms of information — soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure — and are often combined with architectural compression, data augmentation, or privacy-preserving mechanisms. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can improve generalization beyond mere compression, but outcomes depend strongly on what is distilled, teacher–student compatibility, access to (or synthesis of) data, and optimization choices. Practical pipelines therefore blend signal design (logits vs. features), data strategies, and task-aware architecture choices to balance efficiency and retained performance.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods are widely used to convert large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment. Research spanning logit-based supervision, intermediate-feature imitation, attention and relation matching, architecture-aware compression, and data-free or teacher-ensemble schemes has produced many practical recipes. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance across NLP and vision tasks while enabling substantial reductions in parameters and inference latency. Remaining challenges include aligning teacher and student representations, operating without original training data, and choosing distillation targets that best match student capacity and downstream task constraints.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models into smaller, more deployable student models. KD methods operate at multiple levels — output logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure — and are commonly combined with architecture-level compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and training strategies (online co-training, curriculum schedules, synthetic-data protocols). Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while improving latency and memory usage, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and appropriate choice of transfer signal. Ongoing challenges include robust transfer under distribution shift, aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, and operating in data-limited or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Mechanisms, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller students that are deployable under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what to transfer (logits, intermediate representations, relational signals), aligning teacher and student architectures and tokenization, and combining KD with complementary techniques such as architecture search or targeted pruning—distillation routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance and sometimes even improve generalization. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on data availability, teacher quality and friendliness, domain shifts, and the specific form of knowledge chosen for transfer. Effective deployment therefore requires principled design of the distillation objective, curricula or annealing schedules, and safeguards for robustness and rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Indispensable but Contextual Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the original performance. KD has proven effective across modalities and tasks, and modern practice extends beyond simple logit matching to include intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher fusion, data-free approaches, and training-time strategies that make teachers more amenable to transfer. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all solution: distribution shifts, limited or absent training data, teacher–student mismatch, and adversarial concerns require complementary techniques and careful design. When combined with task-aware selection of distilled signals, student-friendly teacher training, and data- or representation-aware remedies, KD becomes a practical backbone for deployment under latency, compute, and privacy constraints.
