papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Effectiveness, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers in both vision and natural language tasks. Empirical work shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints, and many variants extend KD beyond soft-target transfer to feature matching, multi-teacher schemes, progressive replacement, and domain-adaptive workflows. At the same time, theoretical and empirical analyses reveal optimization barriers, sensitivity to the choice of data and teacher signals, and imperfect matching between teacher and student as important limits. This review argues that KD is a powerful but context-dependent tool: its success requires matching the distillation signal to student capacity and task complexity, combining KD with complementary compression techniques, and paying careful attention to data and training dynamics to avoid degenerate outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Bounded Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-strategy approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods include transferring softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and data-free or few-shot variants to handle limited or private data. Best results come from treating KD as one element of a broader compression pipeline that also incorporates architecture-aware choices, data strategies, and explicit attention to robustness and fairness. KD is therefore a central tool for efficient deployment, but it has clear limits and must be designed carefully to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors or losing rare-token performance.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to which signals are transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention), the teacher–student relationship, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD yields substantial efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher behavior. However, KD is not universally sufficient: its success depends on capacity alignment, data and distributional match, and careful objective design. Practical adoption therefore requires selecting KD variants that fit task and system constraints and combining KD with complementary techniques (pretraining, data augmentation, multi-teacher signals, or architecture co-design) to mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of methods for transferring knowledge from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models so that students retain much of the teachers' task performance while reducing inference cost and resource consumption. The practice extends beyond matching final logits to include feature- and layer-level supervision, attention- or projector-based alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware strategies (including data-free or synthetic-data approaches). KD has been applied across modalities and deployment regimes (on-device, privacy-aware, and distributed/federated settings), and empirical work highlights both practical successes and recurring failure modes such as sensitivity to teacher-student mismatch, domain shift, and preservation of rare or low-frequency signals. Current best practices emphasize combining representation-level objectives, careful input/data handling, and co-design of teacher and student; open problems remain around robustness, heterogeneity, and automated student design.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unifying Tool: Compression, Transfer, and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) began as a model compression technique but has evolved into a flexible framework that accomplishes compression, regularization, domain adaptation, continual learning, fairness mitigation, and inductive-bias transfer across architectures and modalities. By choosing what to transfer (logits, features, relations, or module behavior) and how to weight multi-source supervision, practitioners can adapt KD to the constraints and objectives of specific tasks. This paper argues that KD should be treated not merely as a compression trick but as a general-purpose mechanism for shaping student models, and it synthesizes empirical and theoretical evidence to recommend practical best practices for applying KD across modern deep learning and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of methods—logit (soft-target) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, layer- or module-alignment, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, progressive module replacement, online distillation, and data-free generative approaches—has been developed to address different deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, heterogeneous devices). Empirical work shows these techniques can substantially reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but success depends on student capacity, what is transferred, data availability, and task-specific alignment. Open challenges include robust transfer of rare-token behaviors, mitigating transfer of teacher biases, and scaling distillation to privacy- and resource-constrained or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) uses larger or ensemble teacher models to train smaller student models that retain much of the teacher’s predictive ability while reducing inference cost. Over the past decade KD has expanded from matching softened outputs to include intermediate representation matching, layer- and channel-wise guidance, ensemble and multi-teacher approaches, self-distillation, data-free and federated variants, and integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work demonstrates substantial size and latency reductions across vision and NLP with modest accuracy loss when methods are carefully chosen and paired with appropriate data or synthesis strategies. Remaining practical and scientific challenges include robust cross-domain transfer, operating without original training data, mitigating transferred biases, and aligning heterogeneous teacher–student capacities.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels—soft logits, intermediate representations, attention patterns, and relational signals—to enable substantial reductions in size and latency while preserving much teacher performance. Its success in practice depends on careful choice of distillation targets, teacher–student compatibility, data strategies (including synthetic or data-free approaches), and complementary compression methods. KD is powerful but not universal: optimization mismatch, domain shift, and limited data can undermine transfer, so robust pipelines co-design student architectures, distillation signals, and training/data workflows to realize production gains.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information from teacher models. KD encompasses a family of techniques — matching teacher logits (soft targets), aligning intermediate features or attention maps, online or mutual distillation, self-distillation, and data-free or privacy-aware variants — that are routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance in vision and language tasks, but its success depends on teacher quality and specialization, student capacity and architecture, availability and alignment of data, and optimization choices; naive distillation can propagate teacher errors or fail under strong teacher–student mismatch. Practical pipelines therefore select distillation signals and schedules appropriate to task and deployment constraints, often pairing KD with complementary compression techniques to trade compute and size for modest predictive degradation.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely applicable strategy for compressing large neural models by transferring information from one or more high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models. When designed with attention to what is transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals), how teacher and student are aligned, and the data available for training, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of the original performance. KD also integrates naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adapts to specialized settings such as multi-teacher ensembles, heterogeneous-device deployments, generative-model compression, low-precision inference, and privacy-sensitive or data-limited environments. However, KD is not uniformly automatic: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity, distributional match, and design of distillation objectives and curricula.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used and flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teacher models. Over the past decade KD has grown from matching softened output distributions to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, data-free/zero-shot synthesis, and architecture-aware co-design. Empirical work demonstrates KD's ability to reduce parameter counts and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance across vision, speech, and language tasks; its practical success depends on careful choices of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to manage data and augmentation. Remaining challenges include robust distillation under domain shift, preserving rare-token behavior in language models, privacy-sensitive settings, and principled combination of KD with other compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger or more complex models to smaller ones to reduce inference cost, improve deployability, or impart desirable properties (robustness, fairness, interpretability). Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, ensemble consensus, attention maps) and in what data is available (original training data, synthetic data, or no data). Practical systems combine KD with architecture-level compression (pruning, structured sparsity) and with training-time strategies (online or continual distillation, curriculum schedules) to trade off efficiency and accuracy. While KD yields strong empirical results across NLP, speech, vision, and generative models, open challenges remain in data-free settings, cross-domain generalization, preserving fairness and interpretability, and designing distillation objectives that best capture the teacher’s knowledge for a given task.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary practices—such as pretraining compact students, representation-level matching, curriculum scheduling, teacher ensembles, and data augmentation—KD yields strong tradeoffs between efficiency and performance across modalities and tasks. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data or domain mismatch; KD therefore functions best as a central, flexible component within a broader compression pipeline rather than as a one-size-fits-all cure.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis from Selected Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across modalities and tasks, researchers have developed a spectrum of KD mechanisms — soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and progressive schedules, and task- or deployment-aware pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture design. Empirical evidence shows that carefully designed distillation can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude reductions in inference cost, but success depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, the availability and nature of distillation data, and task-specific considerations (e.g., preserving fine-grained sequence behavior or relational structure). Privacy, heterogeneity of deployment devices, and data-scarce regimes motivate variants with differential privacy, few-shot or cross-layer schemes, and heterogeneous multi-model sharing to ensure inclusive and practical compression.

papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD variants transfer information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and adversarially or synthetically generated inputs. When combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, or data strategies, KD supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, success depends on careful matching of what is transferred to student capacity, handling data scarcity or distribution shift, and mitigating propagation of teacher errors. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, representative algorithmic families, empirical patterns, and actionable recommendations for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used approach to compress large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Research shows KD is a flexible toolkit: it can transfer final outputs (soft logits), intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and can be combined with architectural compression (pruning, quantization) or training strategies (online distillation, multi-teacher schedules). Empirical successes span classification, retrieval, reading comprehension, and large-scale language modeling, but outcomes depend strongly on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and optimization design. Important open problems include data-free distillation, cross-domain generalization, robustness and fairness preservation, and automated co-design of teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Methods and Challenges in Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger, more expensive teacher models to smaller, faster student models. Across vision, generative modeling, and NLP, researchers have developed logit- and feature-level distillation, task-specific adaptations, multi-teacher schemes, and teacher-optimization strategies to improve student accuracy, robustness, and efficiency. Work also focuses on constraints arising in distributed and privacy-preserving settings, on preserving rare or fine-grained information, and on adapting distillation to complex tasks such as detection, generation, and dense prediction. Practical systems combine architectural choices, training curricula, and distilled supervision to achieve favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable family of techniques that transfer information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving predictive performance. KD methods differ in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational structure) and how training proceeds (offline teacher supervision, online/co-distillation, self-distillation, or data-free synthesis). Practical deployments combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and require attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability, and task-specific choices. Empirical evidence shows KD reliably yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, but success depends on optimization dynamics, the choice of distilled signals, and constraints such as access to original training data or deployment hardware.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have become practical tools to reduce model size and computation while retaining much of the performance of large teachers. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, approaches include transferring soft logits, mimicking internal features or attention maps, layering/structural adaptations, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or privacy-preserving methods. Empirical results demonstrate that careful distillation can yield compact students that approach teacher accuracy and enable deployment in resource-constrained settings, but open challenges remain in robustness, task-specific distillation design, and distributed training dynamics.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted set of techniques for compressing large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students that retain much of the teachers' performance. Modern KD extends beyond soft-label matching to include representation-level objectives, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, data-free or zero-shot variants, and architecture-aware combinations with pruning, quantization, and search. KD has been applied successfully across domains — including language generation, ranking, detection, and federated settings — but its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to manage data, privacy, and distributional shift. Practical deployment requires selecting distillation signals and training regimes that match student capacity and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multi‑Strategy Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to compressing large models into smaller, efficient students. When treated as a toolbox of complementary methods—logit-level supervision, representation matching, layer alignment, multi-teacher schedules, data synthesis, and privacy-aware mechanisms—KD enables compact models to approach the performance of larger teachers while meeting real-world constraints on latency, memory, and data access. At the same time, distillation outcomes depend on teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and optimization choices; addressing these limits requires careful method selection and integration with complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or multi-modal models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural insights. Research has developed diverse KD variants—soft-label distillation, internal and layer-wise imitation, task-aware filtering, data-free distillation, and architecture-search guided compression—each addressing optimization, data availability, or deployment constraints. Empirical and theoretical work highlights trade-offs between matching teacher outputs and student generalization, the value of pre-training compact models, and the importance of choosing what and how knowledge is transferred to maximize downstream task performance while meeting resource limits.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teachers. KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer schemes that mimic intermediate representations, attention, or relational signals, and it can be combined with pretraining, data augmentation, multi-teacher schedules, and architecture search. Practical effectiveness depends on aligning teacher signals to student capacity, managing limited or private data, and choosing inputs and objectives that preserve fine-grained behaviors. The following synthesis summarizes prevailing mechanisms, representative techniques, empirical strengths and failure modes, and practical recommendations for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: The Practical Case for Knowledge Distillation in NLP: Effectiveness, Mechanisms, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques are a practical and necessary pathway to deploy high-performing pre-trained language models in resource-constrained settings. Distillation enables large teacher models to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations to smaller students, preserving much of the original performance while reducing inference cost. However, the success of distillation depends on choices across pre-training, teacher strength, layer- and feature-level alignment, data used for transfer, and augmentation or curriculum strategies. When these components are designed together, distilled models can approach teacher-level performance and enable real-world NLP systems at lower latency and cost.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of techniques that transfer information from larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models to enable deployment under resource, latency, privacy, or device constraints. KD methods operate across multiple knowledge channels (soft logits, internal features, attention/relations, layer mappings), and they are often combined with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data synthesis). Empirical work shows distilled students can often recover the bulk of teacher performance while reducing compute and memory substantially, but effectiveness depends on task, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and distributional shifts. Important open problems remain in data-free distillation, few-shot compression, preserving rare-token behaviors and robustness, and designing distillation as a system-level primitive matched to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation: Task-adaptive, Privacy-aware, and Feature-centric Compression for Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are now essential tools to deploy large deep models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. When applied thoughtfully—adapting to task requirements, leveraging feature-level signals, and accounting for data availability—KD can yield compact models that retain much of the teacher's performance while improving inference speed, memory footprint, and interpretability. However, naive distillation can fail under data heterogeneity, limited data, or strong teacher–student mismatches; addressing these requires task-aware layer selection, multi-teacher strategies, and alternatives to standard logit matching. I argue that the most effective KD pipelines combine task-adaptive compression, feature-directed supervision, and methods that preserve privacy and robustness to limited data.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students for deployment in constrained environments. KD can transfer predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and structural inductive biases; it supports multi-teacher, progressive, adversarial, and data-constrained variants; and it can be combined with architecture-aware design and data strategies to improve efficiency, robustness, and domain adaptability. While highly effective in practice, KD's success depends on choices about what to transfer, how teachers and students are aligned, and the availability and suitability of data, so it should be treated as a flexible toolkit rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core practical method for producing compact, efficient models across NLP and other modalities. KD transfers information from larger teacher models to smaller students through soft targets, representation- or attention-level imitation, and ensemble or data-synthesis strategies. When combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware training, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, compute, and latency while often preserving—or in some cases improving—task performance. Practical deployment requires attention to teacher quality, data availability, teacher–student architectural mismatch, and privacy constraints, and recent work develops strategies to address these issues.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, deployable pathway to shrink large models while retaining most of their predictive power. When treated as a central design primitive and combined with representation-level objectives, data strategies, and architecture-aware choices, KD enables substantial gains in latency, memory, and deployability across tasks from classification and sequence generation to detection and lifelong learning. However, reliable deployment requires careful attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability and augmentation, and task-specific adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted set of techniques for compressing large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students that retain much of the teachers' performance. Modern KD extends beyond soft-label matching to include representation-level objectives, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, data-free or zero-shot variants, and architecture-aware combinations with pruning, quantization, and search. KD has been applied successfully across domains — including language generation, ranking, detection, and federated settings — but its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to manage data, privacy, and distributional shift. Practical deployment requires selecting distillation signals and training regimes that match student capacity and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: The Centrality of Knowledge Distillation in Modern Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational technique for compressing large neural models while retaining much of their performance. Across vision and language tasks, distillation can act both as a compression mechanism and as a regularizer, and it integrates naturally with complementary strategies such as architecture search, layer-wise alignment, representation matching, data augmentation, pruning, and deployment-aware methods. When applied thoughtfully—matching teacher and student representations, tuning the signal provided by soft labels, and adapting to task or device constraints—distillation enables practical, high-performing compressed models suitable for production and edge settings.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer information from larger, more expensive models (teachers) into smaller, cheaper models (students) to reduce inference cost, enable deployment in constrained environments, or impart desirable properties such as robustness or interpretability. Across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks, researchers have developed a spectrum of KD strategies — from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate features, attention, or relational signals — and combined these with architecture-level compression, pretraining, and data-management strategies. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often approach teacher performance, but success depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation target, data availability, and training dynamics. Open problems include reliable distillation without original data, transferring inductive biases and robustness, and handling heterogeneous or federated data and models.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single recipe for shrinking large models: it is a versatile family of techniques that can preserve performance while enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings, but it must be adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints. Effective KD requires attention to the teacher-student relationship (including training teachers that are "student-friendly"), to data availability (including data-free approaches), and to distributional mismatches (e.g., federated or heterogeneous-device scenarios). When such concerns are addressed—via task-adaptive compression, feature- or relation-aware transfer, multi-teacher or ensemble signals, or methods that expose raw data signals lost in naive distillation—KD can deliver near-teacher performance at far lower cost. However, KD has known failure modes (such as propagating teacher errors on low-frequency tokens or degrading under data heterogeneity) that demand targeted remedies. This paper argues that KD should be treated as an adaptable design pattern: choose techniques that match your downstream objective (accuracy, latency, privacy, heterogeneity) rather than applying a one-size-fits-all distillation loss.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic into a practical, multi-purpose toolkit for compressing large models while preserving performance across domains and modalities. KD enables deployment of powerful models on resource-constrained devices, supports domain adaptation, helps preserve privacy, and can be adapted to architectures ranging from transformers to GANs and GNNs. Complementary techniques — e.g., architectural replacement, data augmentation, multi-teacher schemes, and precision reduction — expand KD’s effectiveness. However, KD’s success depends on how knowledge is represented and transferred (logits, internal representations, relations) and on availability or synthesis of appropriate data. The balance of method and setting determines whether KD yields compact models that meet real-world constraints without unacceptable loss of fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from larger, richer teacher models to smaller, cheaper student models to enable deployment under compute, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature encompasses simple soft-label matching, richer supervision signals that align intermediate features or attention, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-preserving designs, and combinations with structural compression such as pruning and layer skipping. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation can both compress and regularize models, but effectiveness depends on teacher-student mismatch, data availability, and optimization choices; practical pipelines therefore combine multiple compression mechanisms, careful signal selection, and task-aware adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single teacher→student soft-label transfer into a broad toolkit for compressing and adapting deep models across vision, language, and multimodal domains. Contemporary approaches extend logits matching to representation- and structure-aware objectives, multi- and continual-teaching schemes, task-aware layer selection, and combinations with pruning or architecture-level compression. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain-shift constraints but its success depends on design choices about what is transferred, how the student is supervised, data availability, and student capacity. Practical progress emphasizes representation matching beyond logits, careful layer- and channel-level alignment, and composing KD with other compression techniques; remaining challenges include robustness under distribution shift, data-free scenarios, and preserving fine-grained or safety-critical behavior.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a predominant strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. Across vision, language, speech, and other modalities, KD encompasses soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention imitation, relational and training-dynamics transfer, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. When integrated with architecture-level compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful teacher–student co-design, KD enables substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss and can sometimes improve robustness or generalization. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align layers and representations, data availability, and safeguards for fairness and privacy; these constitute active areas of empirical and methodological work.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable smaller or faster models to retain much of the performance of larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or task-specific inductive biases. Work in this area spans supervised soft-target matching, intermediate-layer representation transfer, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free distillation, multi-teacher and ensemble-derived strategies, and online/distributed variants that exploit parallelism. Applications include compressing large pretrained language models for downstream NLP tasks, accelerating inference for computer vision and generative models, and producing interpretable or privacy-preserving compact models for healthcare and on-device deployment. Important trade-offs involve what form of knowledge is transferred (logits, activations, relations), access to training data, robustness to domain heterogeneity, and how to balance capacity, efficiency, and generalization in student models.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Bounded Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and natural language tasks. KD techniques — from logits matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher schedules, adversarial and data-free variants — enable large reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher's performance. However, realizing these gains in practice requires task- and student-aware design choices, attention to data and privacy constraints, and explicit strategies to mitigate transferred fragilities. KD is therefore an essential tool in the compression toolbox, but not a universal remedy: careful method selection and evaluation under deployment constraints determine success.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Compressing and Deploying Large NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible approach to compress large deep models so they can be deployed under latency, storage, and privacy constraints. By transferring predictive behavior and intermediate representations from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student, KD enables large pre-trained NLP models to be adapted, accelerated, and sometimes even improved for downstream tasks and specific domains. Effective KD requires careful design choices—how to match intermediate layers, whether to rely on data or synthesize surrogates, how to combine multiple teachers, and how to account for fairness and domain shift. When combined with complementary compression techniques, KD becomes a core component of production-ready model compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to which signals are transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention), the teacher–student relationship, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD yields substantial efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher behavior. However, KD is not universally sufficient: its success depends on capacity alignment, data and distributional match, and careful objective design. Practical adoption therefore requires selecting KD variants that fit task and system constraints and combining KD with complementary techniques (pretraining, data augmentation, multi-teacher signals, or architecture co-design) to mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central for deploying large deep models in latency- or resource-constrained settings. Across NLP and broader deep learning applications, researchers have developed logit-based distillation, feature- and attention-level mimicking, ensemble- and multi-teacher schemes, task-adaptive compression, and data- or teacher-free variants. These methods trade off compute, memory, and sometimes robustness or fairness, and are often complementary to pruning and architecture search. Practical adoption favors combinations of pretraining, targeted distillation objectives, and adaptations to mismatches between teacher and student (e.g., inputs or architecture).

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and distributed settings KD often recovers much of a teacher's predictive performance while enabling faster inference, lower memory use, and deployment under resource or privacy constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: outcomes depend on what signals are transferred (logits, features, attention), teacher–student compatibility, availability and quality of data (including data-free or federated setups), and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Best practice treats distillation as one element of a compression pipeline that combines representation matching, architecture-aware student design, data strategies, and risk-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information from one or more teachers. Across vision and language applications, KD has been adapted to handle teacher-free scenarios, multi-teacher setups, intermediate representation alignment, data- and domain-shift, and task-specific constraints such as ranking or retrieval. Empirical work shows that distillation can preserve much of teacher performance while dramatically reducing model size and latency, but practical success depends on what is transferred (soft outputs, internal features, or relational/contrastive knowledge), the quality and heterogeneity of teacher data, and training design choices such as data augmentation and curriculum. The literature also highlights cases where naive distillation propagates teacher errors (e.g., low-frequency lexical mistakes) and where alternative strategies (label smoothing view, internal representation matching, dynamic teacher weighting, or curriculum selection of examples) yield measurable improvements. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, common pitfalls, and promising methods for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.
